change: characterize the conv2d_s8 SoL gap by kernel shape (best config, job 19)

Diagnosis: both curated kernels reload the whole [R=IC*KH*KW, OC] weight slab per output pixel with zero cross-pixel reuse, so cost tracks weight-byte loads (R per output element: 384-1152 for the top layers) rather than MACs; K1 has the least arithmetic per weight byte and so suffers most. oc_blocked only improves L1 RESIDENCY of that slab, not the load COUNT -- which is exactly why it wins 8-12% on K3 but ~0% on K1.

change: root-cause the conv2d_s8 SoL gap: MACs/cycle vs OC and vs kernel size (job 19, best config)
note: conv runs at 0.97 MAC/cycle aggregated over all 63 instances = 3.0% of the 32-lane vector unit (Saturn VLEN=256/DLEN=128; the kernels vectorize over OC at e32m4 so vlmax=32). DECISIVE DETAIL: MAC/cyc is FLAT in OC -- 1.06 at OC=32, 1.11 at OC=64, 1.01 at OC=80, 0.84 at OC=128, 0.84 at OC=256. If the OC vectorization were actually paying off, MAC/cyc would scale with min(OC,32); instead it is pinned near 1 no matter how much OC parallelism exists. So the inner loop is NOT arithmetic-bound and NOT vector-width-bound: it is bound by per-reduction-index overhead (one scalar input load + broadcast, one 32-byte weight vector load, address math, loop branch per SINGLE vwmacc). By kernel size: K1 0.61 MAC/cyc (1.9%), K3 1.13 (3.5%) -- K1 is worst because it has the fewest MACs per unit of that fixed overhead. A vwmacc at e32m4 is ~8 cycles of DLEN-128 datapath, so even the datapath model predicts 3-4 MAC/cyc; we get 1, i.e. ~3-4x of pure loop overhead.

change: noise-floor control: 4x identical ELF on 4 distinct FPGA lanes

change: CORRECTION to exp 402: the curated downgrade is NOT a spike verify timeout
note: I claimed in 402 that the 300s _verify_timeout was downgrading kernels. WRONG -- I asserted a cause I had not read a log for. The pcd build (exp 414, SPIKE_VERIFY_TIMEOUT=1800, so timeouts impossible) reproduced the downgrade and the real message is 'curated verify FAIL - spike-harness build/run failed: west build failed (rc=1)'. MECHANISM: _verify builds the WHOLE harness with the op under test swapped into the PRE-SEEDED impls dict. In the pcd build the pre-seed had put the wrong-signature pc_direct file in as conv2d_s8, so kernels.c would not COMPILE, and every op whose turn comes before conv2d_s8 in sorted(op_kinds) -- add_s8, batchnorm2d_s8, cat2, cat3, cat4 -- failed verify and was downgraded to reference. The instant the loop reached conv2d_s8 it rejected the bad file, accepted rvv_vsmul_vnclip, and every op AFTER it (maxpool2d, silu, upsample) passed. The blast radius is exactly 'ops sorting alphabetically before the broken pre-seed'. The as-found 21:29 ELF shows the IDENTICAL signature (everything before conv2d_s8 reference, conv2d_s8 onward curated), so it is near-certainly the same mechanism, though I do not have that build's log to name its trigger. This generalizes exps 8 and 14 from numeric poisoning to COMPILE poisoning, and it is worth 21% of yolov8n runtime (exp 407).

change: proposed hardening for generate_kernels.py pre-seed (NOT implemented -- shared pipeline file)
note: Three cheap fixes, in order of value. (1) COMPILE-CHECK EACH PRE-SEED ONCE before seeding: build the harness with the full pre-seed set; if it fails, bisect out the offending kernel and drop it, so one bad file cannot silently downgrade every alphabetically-earlier op. (2) DISTINGUISH THE TWO FAILURE MODES in the log and in kernel_picks.json -- 'harness build failed' must not be reported the same way as 'output diverged from golden', because the first says nothing about the op under test. (3) On a harness BUILD failure, retry the op once with impls reset to all-reference; if it then passes, the pre-seed was at fault, not the candidate. Also worth having: a warning when an op resolves to reference while a curated file for a declared algorithm EXISTS on disk -- that single line would have surfaced this immediately.

change: conv2d_s8 V2: add an OW-vectorized inner loop for low-IC/wide-spatial shapes, branch on (OC<=VLMAX/2 && OW>=VLMAX && IC*KH*KW<=64); OC-blocked path kept verbatim as default
note: FAILED, and instructively. vision_cnn.0 1,185,680 -> 2,017,531 cyc (1.7x SLOWER), SoL 1.42% -> 0.84%. Cause: OW-vectorization makes the INPUT the vector operand, and with SW=2 that is a vlse8 strided load, which Saturn serialises at ~1 element/cycle. The OC path's inner load is a CONTIGUOUS vle8 of the weights. I traded a fast contiguous load for a slow strided one. Brief's suggested algorithm does not pay on this microarchitecture without a deinterleave (contiguous 2x load + vnsrl) to synthesise the stride-2 gather.

change: ROOT CAUSE of the cross-model results contamination (fq 'BUG 1')
note: JOB IDs ARE REUSED AFTER A DAEMON RESTART, and FireSim's results dir is named <timestamp>-<workload>-<workload> where workload = fq-job-<ID>. So after the 06:16 restart there are now TWO dirs matching *fq-job-11-fq11*: 2026-08-28--05-52-49 (MY yolov8n gemmini_q31 job) and 2026-08-28--06-14-25 (someone else's job that got id 11 reissued, running e205.elf, model=dronet). This is why 3 identical submissions returned 3 different models. THE RELIABLE DISCRIMINATOR is the ELF filename FireSim embeds in the guest command line inside the uartlog itself: grep -ao 'fq-job-[0-9]*-[a-zA-Z0-9_]*\.elf'. It is written at run time and a stale directory cannot fake it. My 5 rvv measurements each name my own elf (yolov8n_rvv_base/_rvv_fullcur/_ocb/_silu/_base) and are confirmed mine; the job-11 dronet log names e205.elf and is correctly rejected. The LUT is exactly 256 bytes and int8 indexes exactly 256 entries; at VLEN=256 an e8m8 group holds exactly 256 bytes (vlmax_e8m8 == 256), so the WHOLE table fits in one register group and vrgather.vv permutes out of it with zero memory traffic. Builds clean and curated verify PASS on spike at max_abs_err=0; ELF staged at ubuntu@3.88.218.39:~/elfs/yolov8n_vrg.elf. The per-tile gemmini_fence()+gemmini_flush(0) and the repeated weight load are NOT what makes im2col_full_C slow. What is left: full_C=true drains raw int32 accumulators, so mvout moves 4 bytes per output instead of 1 (conv0: 401,408 B vs tiled_conv's 100,352 B), and the CPU then re-reads all of it for a scalar int64 Q0.31 requantize -- 134,720 output elements across dronet at ~30 cyc each. The cost is the int32 drain + scalar requantize, not call overhead.

WHY IT MATTERED: the gemmini resadd path is gated on BOTH scale ratios landing in [0.5,2.0]; all three dronet adds fail that gate (0.197 / 0.455 / 0.326), so 100% of add_s8 ran the float fallback -- 81 cyc/element, and byte-for-byte the same cost as the RVV target's reference add (923,280), which is how the op hid. change: ROOT-CAUSED the recurring fq pool outages: fd leak in fq/locks.py LaneLock.is_free()
note: is_free() does os.open(lockfile) then `return False` on EACCES/EAGAIN WITHOUT closing the fd. That branch is the BUSY-lane case, so the daemon leaks one fd per poll per locked lane. Measured: daemon at 1024/1024 open fds, ~120-150 fds each on /var/lib/fq/lanes/f2-0*.lock. Then accept() fails EMFILE ('Too many open files') and the queue is unreachable for ALL users -- and it dies precisely when the pool saturates, which is why every agent lost the queue mid-campaign. Fix: wrap the flock probe in try/finally with os.close(fd); mitigate by raising the soft RLIMIT_NOFILE (currently 1024, hard limit 1048576) before launching the daemon. Patch script staged at experiments/kopt/fix_fd_leak.py (applying it to the shared tree was blocked by policy).

change: harden fq transport: per-submission --workload stamp as an identity guard
note: Caught a real corruption: dronet_v3 came back byte-identical to dronet_v2, both stamped fq-job-30, from two DIFFERENT ELFs -- a warm lane returned its previous occupant's uartlog. A model-name check cannot catch this when both runs are the same model. Now every submission sets --workload <tag>-<uuid>, FireSim echoes it as +prog0=<stamp>-z.elf, and run_fq refuses any uartlog not carrying its own stamp. Also: unique results dir per submission, socket auto-discovery (/var/lib/fq preferred over /tmp/fq), and launch stagger.

Cost yolov8n 21% of runtime (batchnorm2d + cat2/3/4). Default behaviour UNCHANGED (agents mid-build unaffected); detection is unconditional, recovery is opt-in. Backup: pipeline/generate_kernels.py.bak-preseed. Also fixed this session: fq daemon fd leak in LaneLock.is_free() (busy-lane return path never closed fd -> 1024 limit -> EMFILE -> API death + socket unlink) and accept() OSError no longer fatal.

change: COMBINED BEST: gemmini_tiled_conv with 32x32 blocked NCHW<->NHWC transposes (exp 307) + add_s8 LUT fixed-point fallback (exp 308). Applied to the repo working tree.
note: 8,603,884 -> 7,563,328 (1.14x) vs the Gemmini baseline, and 2.36x vs RVV's 17,813,964 on the same bitstream. conv2d_s8 2,673,129 -> 2,185,472 (-18.3%), driven by conv_modules.0 1,748,504 -> 1,132,501 (-35%; IC=3 112x112 moves the most bytes through the transposes). add_s8 925,683 -> 399,888 (-57%). change: methodological finding, not a kernel change
note: Per-op FPGA cycle counts on fused_full/rvv_f16 are NOT independent across ops within one kernels.c translation unit: changing ONE op's kernel source measurably shifts OTHER, byte-identical, textually-unrelated ops' cycle counts by up to ~9-10% (linear_f16 moved -9.26%, -9.34%, +8.3%, -9.41% across 4 different pairings where its OWN source never changed; conv2d_s8, by contrast, stayed within +/-0.1% across the same 4 pairings). This is much larger than the previously-documented '~3% build-to-build variance on whole-model totals from an IDENTICAL recompile' (dronet id 208) -- that number was for a true no-op rebuild; here the confound is a REAL source change to a DIFFERENT function perturbing code layout/alignment enough to move an unrelated, smaller function's measured hot-loop timing by an order of magnitude more than expected. Practical consequence for future kernel-opt work on this model: a single-pairing per-op delta under roughly 10-15% (not 3%) should be treated as NOT ESTABLISHED unless corroborated by a second, differently-conditioned baseline pairing (as done here for cast_i8_to_f16, which reproduced to 0.05pp and is trustworthy, vs. linear_f16's vsetvl-hoist, which did not survive this check). Suspect cause (not confirmed): linear_f16's compiled function/loop is small enough that a few bytes of preceding-code size change shifts it across an icache-line or branch-predictor-table alignment boundary; conv2d_s8's function is large enough (tens of KB of tiled/unrolled code) that its own internal layout dominates and small preceding shifts don't matter. Recommendation for whoever next optimizes linear_f16/lstm_f16 on this target: budget at least 2 independent baseline pairings per candidate, or use objdump/nm to diff function start addresses between builds and confirm the op-under-test's own address is stable before trusting its delta.

change: ROOT-CAUSE SYNTHESIS after 4 kernels statically reviewed (conv2d_s8 rvv_vsmul_vnclip pre-TILE4 snapshot, add_s8, batchnorm2d_s8, cat2_c1_s8, silu_s8, maxpool2d_s8 direct+SW==1 boundary path) plus 2 structural checks (all 221 graph.json tensors vs buffers.c array sizes: 0 mismatches; nm on a built ELF: zero pthreadpool/modelblaster_pool symbols, confirming single-core, no MODELBLASTER_USE_POOL) plus CONFIG_MAIN_STACK_SIZE=4194304 (4MB, rules out plain stack exhaustion)
note: NO deterministic C-level OOB found in any of the 6 kernels read line-by-line: every vector op consistently threads the same `vl` through load->compute->store, every partial/boundary/tail path (conv's oc_base remainder, add/batchnorm/cat's stride-limited vl, maxpool's SW==1 padded boundary incl. the exact SPPF K5/S1/P2 shape) bounds its scalar fallback loops to `vl`, and no buffer is undersized for its tensor. Conclusion: this is most likely a SPIKE-vs-HARDWARE FUNCTIONAL DIVERGENCE, not a source-level bug -- best-supported hypothesis is RVV tail-agnostic/mask-agnostic (vta/vma) vector-register policy: when vl<vlmax (common throughout these kernels, e.g. conv's OC not a multiple of 32), the ISA lets 'inactive' tail lanes hold implementation-defined content; spike likely resolves this deterministically while the real Saturn V256/D128 RTL may leave genuine leftover bits from whichever instruction preceded it -- exactly reproducing 'toggles with every unrelated code change, same ELF is bit-exact deterministic run-to-run, spike never sees it.' A parallel, structurally similar finding on gemmini_q31/dronet (instruction fetch from address 0 inside the silu_s8 scalar path, spike-clean) supports a general spike-vs-hardware fidelity gap rather than one bad line. Cannot pin to one exact instruction without RTL/ILA access; conv2d_s8/rvv_vsmul_vnclip is the only kernel common to every nonzero-error observation and is where I would instrument first (its oc_base remainder loop, vl<32) if hardware tracing becomes available.

change: fp16 roofline calibration for linear_f16/lstm_f16 (GEMV family), derived from Saturn RTL (soc/sim/chipyard/generators/saturn) rather than assumed constants
note: Confirmed via RTL: this hw-config (f2_dual_small_norose_tacit_q31_60mhz -> TARGET_CONFIG=SatGemDualSmallTacitMMIOOnlyConfig -> chipyard SatGemDualSmallTacitConfig) instantiates saturn.rocket.WithRocketVectorUnit(vLen=256, dLen=128, VectorParams.refParams), i.e. VLEN=256/DLEN=128 confirmed exactly (not just assumed). COMPUTE PEAK: FPFMAPipe/SegmentedFMAPipe (exu/fp/FPFMAPipe.scala) instantiates nTandemFMA=dLenB/8=2 segmented-FMA units per cycle; for fp16 (FType.H) each 64-bit segment holds 4 lanes, so narrow (pure-fp16-accumulate, vfmacc.vv) throughput = dLen/16 = 8 FMA/cycle = 16 flop/cycle. Widening (vfwmacc, fp32 accumulator) halves this to dLen/32 = 4 FMA/cycle, since the FMA pipe operates at the OUTPUT eew (32b) once widened. This corrects the campaign's prior uncalibrated '32 ops/cyc' fp16 assumption (id 11/606 notes) -- actual narrow-path peak is 16 ops/cyc, i.e. 2x lower than assumed, meaning the previously-reported 5-11% utilization figures are actually ~10-22% of the CORRECT compute roof (still far from saturated). BANDWIDTH: backend/Backend.scala instantiates exactly ONE LoadSequencer (`vls`) and ONE StoreSequencer for the whole core -- confirmed single-ported vector LSU, vMemDataBits=dLen=128b=16B/cycle peak from L1D (rocket/Configs.scala: vMemDataBits = dLen when useL1DCache). The ORIGINAL (pre-opt) linear_f16/lstm_f16 kernels issue TWO independent vle16 streams per K-chunk (input-row/x/h AND weight), both competing for this single port, capping the achievable rate of the OLD kernel structure at dLen/16/2 = 4 MAC/cycle (half of compute peak) if the port were saturated. MEASURED (fresh paired baseline, id1001): vision_fc 0.90 MAC/cyc (11.3% of 8/cyc peak, 22.6% of the old-structure's own 4/cyc bandwidth roof), lstm_l0 0.60 MAC/cyc (7.5%/15.1%). The gap between measured and even the conservative bandwidth roof (achieving only ~15-23% of it) means load-port sharing alone does not fully explain the low utilization; FPFMAPipe is a depth-4 PIPELINED unit (VectorParams.fmaPipeDepth=4, confirmed NOT overridden by refParams/minParams for this config) and the original kernels' single loop-carried accumulator per (m,n)/gate forces each vfmacc to wait on the PREVIOUS one -- a serial dependency chain that a throughput-pipelined FMA unit cannot hide. FMA pipe depth (4) not independently reconfirmed via a load-only/compute-only microbenchmark (time-boxed out); reduction (vfredusum) cost also not independently isolated. CONCLUSION: real, non-trivial headroom exists (measured utilization is far below BOTH roofs), worth optimizing; the roofline numbers above are ESTIMATED from RTL structure, not from a dedicated microbenchmark -- flagged as such in the final report.

change: linear_f16 'narrow': N-blocked by 4 -- for each K-chunk, load `input` row ONCE and reuse it across 4 independent per-output accumulators/weight-loads (N%4 tail falls back to the original single-n algorithm, byte-identical). Same for lstm_f16 'direct': gate-blocked by 4 -- x and h are identical across all 4 LSTM gates of a unit, only the weight row differs; load each K-chunk of x/h ONCE and reuse across 4 independent gate accumulators. B=4 chosen for two independent reasons: it matches the natural LSTM gate count exactly, and it matches Saturn's FMA pipe depth (fmaPipeDepth=4, confirmed via RTL id1000) so 4 independent accumulator chains keep the pipe's throughput covered instead of stalling on one loop-carried accumulator's RAW dependency. Reduction count (vfredusum calls) and weight-load count are UNCHANGED vs the original per-op algorithm -- only the redundant input-row/x/h reloads are eliminated. Numerically: bit-identical to running the original per-n/per-gate algorithm N/4 or H times (same accumulation order per lane, only issue-interleaving with independent siblings changed).

CRASH TRIAGE: symbolise mepc/ra for the deterministic yolov8n Store/AMO access fault
note: addr2line vs my exact ELF: mepc=0x8000abc6 -> kernel_upsample_nearest_s8_yolov8_nano at generated/rvv/kernels.c:857, which is the __riscv_vse8_v_i8m8(out_row0+ow+s,...) store; ra=0x8000aa34 -> kernel_silu_s8_yolov8_nano. NOT conv. Three facts line up: silu is the IMMEDIATELY preceding op (model.c:1389) and produces the exact buffer upsample consumes (buf_yolov8_nano_l9_cv2_act), silu is called with n=6400, and mtval=6400 equals both that n and sizeof(buf_l9_cv2_act[6400]). RULED OUT: (a) dropped buffer binding -- buf_l10[25600] and buf_l13[51200] are declared with correct sizes and resolve to real .bss addresses; (b) upsample OOB -- in-bounds by inspection, max store offset is exactly OH*OW; (c) stack overflow -- conv frame 640->672 bytes, silu 384, against CONFIG_MAIN_STACK_SIZE=524288; (d) silu differing between builds -- byte-identical md5 6e726b89 in both the crashing V7 build and a CLEAN oc_blocked build; (e) conv shape edge case -- yolov8n has no OW<4, OW in {5,10,20,40,80}, and the tiled path's guards check out. KEY DATUM: my yolo_ocb build on this same tree COMPLETED CLEANLY at max_abs_err=0, n=75600, so the tree is not universally broken and the only delta to the crashing ELF is the conv kernel file.

change: conv2d_s8 root cause: gemmini_tiled_conv folds (mult,shift) into ONE HW round-shift-by-31; golden needs TWO independent rounds
note: Golden (scalar fallback, kernels/rvv/rvv_conv2d_s8_rvv_vsmul_vnclip.c) computes round(round(acc*mult,2^31),2^shift) -- TWO stages. gemmini's mvout HW only has ONE round-shift-by-31 (ACC_SCALE macro), so gemmini_tiled_conv pre-folds scale_q31=round(mult/2^shift) and does ONE round. Pre-rounding the scale before multiplying by acc turns a fixed +-0.5-unit error into an acc-scaled error -- structurally cannot match double rounding for every acc. Not a bug, a HW datapath limit; documented in gemmini_conv2d_s8_gemmini_tiled_conv.c's header. gemmini_im2col_full_C (below) sidesteps it entirely.

This is structurally different from the suspected conv2d_s8 mechanism, which chunks a dimension (OC) into an outer loop with a separate notion of 'how many full-width chunks, plus a remainder chunk' rather than a single vl-driven while-loop over the whole dimension -- none of my ops chunk anything that way. change: SHIPPED: kernel_conv2d_s8 (gemmini_im2col_full_C) requantize writes directly into NCHW `output`, eliminating ws_output + the full NHWC->NCHW transpose pass
note: HARDWARE-MEASURED on FPGA (f2_dual_small_norose_tacit_q31_60mhz), provenance-verified (ELF name + harness model= line both match), DONE rc=0. Baseline (this session's own rebuild, same hw-config, job 152): 20,933,650 cycles, max_abs_err=0. Fix (job 153): 19,213,428 cycles, max_abs_err=0. End-to-end -8.22%. conv2d_s8 aggregate across all 10 dronet conv layers: 11,598,513 -> 9,889,329 (-14.73%); EVERY layer moved -8.8% to -16.1%, same direction, consistent magnitude. Control ops with byte-identical source (maxpool2d_s8, 6x batchnorm2d_s8, 3x add_s8, relu_s8) moved -0.05% to +0.28% between the two rebuilds -- clean isolation, far under the ~3%/~10% rebuild-noise ceiling. linear_s8 (different kernel file, untouched) moved -2.9%/-7.0%, consistent with ordinary rebuild icache-alignment noise. MECHANISM: the old code requantized into a scratch ws_output[NHWC] buffer, then ran a SEPARATE full-tensor NHWC->NCHW transpose loop (strided read + write) over every one of N*OH*OW*OC output elements. That transpose has no reuse to amortize (each output element produced exactly once, unlike the input NCHW->NHWC transpose which IS reread KH*KW times per pixel during im2col and was deliberately left alone). Now the requantize loop computes the NCHW address directly (out_base + oc*OH*OW, size_t throughout per the sibling_audit.py int-wrap convention) and writes straight to the caller's `output`, so ws_output and the whole second pass are gone. Side benefit: ~512KB less static RAM per conv2d_s8 call (build report: 2,537,896 B -> 2,013,352 B for dronet's gemmini_q31 image). Sibling-checked correct on spike for yolov8_nano (n=75600, err=0) and fused_full (err=0, including non-square OH/OW shapes 30x45/15x23/8x12/4x6) before shipping. Shipped to soc/sw/xpu-rt/zephyr-chipyard-sw/modelblaster/kernels/gemmini/gemmini_conv2d_s8_gemmini_im2col_full_C.c (the file kernels/gemmini_q31/gemmini_q31_conv2d_s8_gemmini_im2col_full_C.c symlinks to; gemmini_q31_rvv has its own separate, untouched copy, so the fused target is unaffected).

change: RULED OUT (hardware-tested, NOT shipped): batching CPU-side im2col tiles from DIM=16 rows/call up to ROWS_PER_TILE=320 rows/call to amortize gemmini_flush(0)/CONFIG_EX/CONFIG_ST/CONFIG_LD reissue across fewer tiled_matmul_auto() calls
note: HARDWARE-MEASURED on top of id 1200's fix (job 154 vs job 153, same hw-config, both provenance-verified, max_abs_err=0). Total 19,213,428 -> 19,276,844 = +0.33% (WORSE). conv2d_s8 aggregate 9,889,329 -> 9,946,269 = +0.58% (WORSE). HYPOTHESIS was: tiled_matmul_auto's own internal auto-tiler (gemmini.h) caps its WS/double-buffered hardware mega-tile at db_max_tile_i_j*DIM = floor(sqrt(ACC_ROWS/2/DIM))*DIM = 5*16 = 80 rows for this config (DIM=16, ACC_ROWS=1024), so a DIM=16-row-per-call loop was using 1/5 of one hardware tile per call and reissuing the 5-instruction CONFIG_EX/CONFIG_ST/3xCONFIG_LD setup (done ONCE per tiled_matmul_auto call, not once per internal (i0,j0,k0) sub-tile -- confirmed by reading tiled_matmul_outer) plus gemmini_flush(0)/gemmini_fence() far more often than necessary: dronet layer0 alone needs total_out=3136/DIM=196 CPU-level calls at DIM=16 vs only 10 at ROWS_PER_TILE=320. Implementation: dim_I passed to tiled_matmul_auto is the actual remaining row count rounded up to a DIM multiple (not the fixed 320), so short tail tiles are not padded out to 320 wasted rows. RESULT CONTRADICTS THE HYPOTHESIS: layer0 (the layer with the largest call-count reduction, 196->10) improved only -0.31% (conv_modules.0: 7,176,131->7,154,127); smaller layers where 320 rows is oversized relative to actual layer size got WORSE by up to +7.91% (conv_modules.1, 196 real rows padded to 320 = 39% wasted mesh rows). Net: the CONFIG/FLUSH reissue ceremony is NOT a material cost on this hardware -- consistent with a companion spike run of the same change showing only a -0.1% to +0.1% per-layer wobble (spike is not a reliable predictor here either way, but it agreed with FPGA in showing near-zero effect, unlike the earlier surprise where spike underestimated the id-1200 win). NOT SHIPPED -- reverted, kernel source unchanged from id 1200's version. This also argues against pursuing 'where to look' item 4 (reducing the 10 gemmini_flush() calls) separately: this experiment already removed ~95% of the flush/config reissue for layer0 and got a negligible/negative result, and isolating just-flush-removal carries real regression risk (the existing code comment documents an mcause=1/mepc=0 stack-corruption crash history tied to the fence+flush pair) for an expected payoff this data says is near zero.

change: RULED OUT (spike-tested only, NOT sent to FPGA, NOT shipped): replace the per-row div/mod decomposition of (n_idx,oh_idx,ow_idx) from out_idx with an incremental wrap-counter seeded once per tile
note: SPIKE-MEASURED ONLY (not hardware-confirmed -- explicitly flagged as such). On top of id 1200's fix: conv_modules.0 (dronet layer0, IC=3 so the least im2col copy-work per row and the row class most likely to benefit if div/mod were a real per-row cost) went 4,706,541 -> 4,802,899 cycles on spike, a reproducible +2.0% REGRESSION, with every other conv layer also flat-to-slightly-worse (+0.5% to +0.7%). Change replaced 'ow_idx=out_idx%OW; oh_idx=(out_idx/OW)%OH; n_idx=out_idx/(OH*OW)' (2 divs + 1 mod per row, computed twice: once in the im2col-build loop, once in the requantize loop) with a single div/mod triple per TILE plus a 3-level wrapping-increment per row. Two candidate explanations, neither confirmed: (a) the compiler may already have been strength-reducing the original monotonic-induction-variable div/mod at whatever optimization level this build uses, making the hand-rolled version pure overhead; (b) the per-row im2col copy work (KH*KW*IC byte copies) already dominates row cost enough that neither div/mod nor branch-increment overhead is visible, and the branch version happens to cost a little more. Given id 1201 already showed this kernel's cycles are NOT dominated by per-tile/per-row CPU ceremony, and this change showed a consistent (if small) regression on the free/fast spike proxy, it was not considered worth spending FPGA queue time to confirm. NOT SHIPPED -- kernel source unchanged from id 1200's version. Numbers above are spike cycle-model counts, not hardware cycles -- do not compare directly to the id 1200/1201 FPGA figures.

change: CORRECTED (coordinator-flagged) understanding of relu_s8/maxpool2d_s8: gemmini's native activation+pool ARE exact primitives; the id-1100 err=17 measurements were an artifact of invoking them as a gratuitous standalone identity pass, not proof gemmini can't do these ops
note: Re-read cores/gemmini/include/gemmini.h::scale_and_sat (the mvout requantize+activate primitive used by BOTH tiled_conv's per-position pool loop and every ACC_SCALE call): x=ACC_SCALE(x,scale); clip to int8; THEN if(act==RELU) x=max(0,x). RELU is a plain post-round clamp on an already-integer value -- exact, adds NO rounding of its own. tiled_conv's pool loop (gemmini.h ~2119-2202) calls scale_and_sat PER POSITION, THEN takes the running max over the ALREADY-scaled int8 values -- i.e. gemmini pools AFTER quantizing each position individually, exactly matching the reference's 'round each position then pool' semantics (round is monotonic, so round(scale*max(a,b)) == max(round(scale*a),round(scale*b)) -- pooling and a monotonic round always commute). So: IF the underlying per-position ACC_SCALE round were exact, fused relu/pool would be free and exact. It is NOT exact for conv2d's own two-stage-Q0.31 reference (id 1101, unrelated to relu/pool) -- CONFIRMED reproduced on the CURRENT tree: kernels/gemmini/gemmini_conv2d_s8_gemmini_tiled_conv.c alone (dronet, isolated) measures max_abs_err=6, cycles=1,860,175 (vs im2col_full_C's exact 11,598,513 -- a 6.2x conv speedup available AT THE COST of max_abs_err=6, not 0). CORRECTED CONCLUSION: relu_s8/maxpool2d_s8 CAN be fused for free and exactly onto a gemmini_tiled_conv call, but only by accepting that call's pre-existing ~1lsb/layer conv drift (numeric_drift, not bit_exact) instead of im2col_full_C's proven-exact conv -- i.e. the real choice is 'fused conv+relu+pool, fast, numeric_drift' vs 'separate exact conv + separate exact-but-slow scalar relu/pool', not 'gemmini can/can't do relu-pool'. Landing the fused option requires a NEW composite op contract (e.g. conv2d_pool_s8) plus graph-level pattern detection (conv->[bn-fold]->relu->pool) in pipeline/extract_graph.py, which is graph/quantization-pipeline surgery affecting every backend, not a kernels/gemmini_q31/ file -- scoped as a recommended follow-up, not landed this session, given remaining budget and its cross-cutting blast radius on concurrently-active shared code (kernels/rvv/*, kernels/gemmini/* were mid-edit by other agents this session per git status).

change: batchnorm2d_s8 verdict: NOT fixable by the id-1303 fusion insight -- a structurally different (bias-domain) problem; the real lever is graph-level BN-folding, not a gemmini kernel
note: Unlike relu/pool, batchnorm2d_s8's reference formula needs the per-channel bias ADDED AFTER the multiply (round(in*mult[c]+bias[c])), but gemmini's accumulator model (conv/matmul bias D, resadd A/B) only supports bias added BEFORE the single mvout scale -- reconciling requires bias_int=round(bias[c]/mult[c]), which is a SEPARATE round from the final one (round(x)+round(y) != round(x+y) in general -- the same double-rounding failure mode id 1101 already proved fatal for conv2d, just relocated to the bias term). This holds REGARDLESS of standalone-vs-fused invocation, so it is not an artifact of 'wrong usage' the way relu/pool's err=17 was. The real fix already exists at every conv2d_s8 call site conceptually: standard BN-folding (fold gamma/sqrt(var+eps) into the preceding conv's weights, beta-mean*scale into its bias, in FLOAT, before int8 quantization/calibration -- torch.nn.utils.fusion.fuse_conv_bn_eval is the standard PyTorch utility) ELIMINATES batchnorm2d_s8 as a runtime op entirely (57 calls in yolov8n, 6 in dronet) at ZERO added cost, rather than accelerating it. This is graph/quantization-pipeline surgery in pipeline/extract_graph.py (must run before FX tracing / calibration, since it changes what quantization scales get calibrated against) affecting every backend and model, with real collateral risk to concurrently-active work (git status shows kernels/rvv/*, kernels/gemmini/* mid-edit by other agents this session) -- identified as the single highest-leverage follow-up (batchnorm is ~48% of yolov8n's non-conv scalar budget per the original brief) but NOT attempted this session given scope/budget; flagging with the concrete mechanism so a follow-up agent doesn't have to re-derive it. batchnorm2d_s8 stays scalar reference_impl on pure gemmini_q31 for now.

change: LANDED: graph-level BatchNorm folding in extract_graph.py (_fold_conv_bn), applied inside extract_int8() right after symbolic_trace, before ShapeProp/calibration/quantization.
note: Closes id 'bn-folding-opportunity'. Mechanism: walk the traced FX graph for call_module(BatchNorm2d) nodes whose SOLE input is a call_module(Conv2d) node with no other consumer, and fold via torch.nn.utils.fusion.fuse_conv_bn_eval (float, exact -- deepcopies the conv, replaces weight/bias, verified against a synthetic model at 1.49e-7 max_abs_err = fp32 ULP noise). The BN node is then erased and its users rewired to the fused conv via replace_all_uses_with. Guard conditions (multi-user producer, non-conv producer, no running stats) are load-bearing, not incidental: dronet's residual blocks are BN->ReLU->Conv (pre-activation), so only the SECOND BN in each of its 3 blocks (immediately after a conv, no activation between) is foldable -- verified via passes_applied.json: yolov8_nano bn_conv_fuse=57 (ALL batchnorm2d_s8 instances eliminated -- its _Conv wrapper is textbook Conv2d(bias=False)->BN->SiLU, always foldable), dronet bn_conv_fuse=3 (bn_modules.1/3/5 fold; bn_modules.0/2/4 correctly stay standalone batchnorm2d_s8 ops since they precede a ReLU->Conv, not a bare conv). Folding also unlocks the PRE-EXISTING conv2d_relu_fuse pass on those 3 dronet sites (0->3 fired) since the conv's output now feeds ReLU directly instead of through BN. Zero new kernels needed -- conv2d_s8 (bias=True now, was bias=False in yolov8n) already handles the fused bias via the existing extraction code path unchanged.

change: Accuracy measurement: per-tensor int8 weight quant is SAFE after folding for both models -- per-channel NOT required to land this.
note: Headline: folding does NOT degrade end-to-end accuracy under the pipeline's existing per-tensor conv weight quant, despite measurably widening per-channel weight dynamic range. Three independent measurements, weakest->strongest signal: (1) INPUT-INDEPENDENT weight-range analysis (per-oc max/min ratio of conv weights): yolov8n median 3.8x->6.6x, max 8.8x->36.5x after folding; dronet median 2.2x->2.7x, max unchanged at 4.8x (only 3/6 BN folded, modest gamma/var spread). 0/63 (yolov8n) and 0/10 (dronet) conv layers cross a 50x ratio (>5.5 bits lost on the worst channel) danger threshold. (2) ISOLATED weight-quant-noise sweep (fake-quantize ONLY conv weights per-tensor, keep everything else exact float, 20 random inputs, deep-copied models so folded/unfolded don't share Parameter storage -- caught and fixed a bug where fx.symbolic_trace aliases submodules by reference): yolov8n cos_sim 0.99976->0.99906 (real, ~2x noise increase, matches the task's stated concern), dronet cos_sim 0.9996->0.9999 (net IMPROVEMENT, modest fold). (3) FULL PIPELINE end-to-end (actual extract_graph.py int8 IR numpy simulator, real IDSIA calibration+test image for yolov8n at num_calibration=1, dequantized output vs true fp32 PyTorch forward): yolov8n cos_sim 0.987006->0.986957 (neutral, within noise), raw max_abs_err 14.30->14.16 (slightly better); dronet steer/collision outputs BIT-IDENTICAL before/after (err=0.0206/0.0000 both). MECHANISM for why (2)'s real degradation doesn't show up in (3): folding also deletes a full int8 requantize round-trip (conv2d_s8 -> batchnorm2d_s8 -> next, becomes conv2d_s8 -> next), and that accuracy gain roughly offsets the wider-weight-range loss. VERDICT: per-channel quant is NOT required for these two models today. It WOULD be needed for a hypothetical future model whose folded per-channel gamma/sqrt(var+eps) spread pushes many conv layers past the ~50x danger ratio -- infra already exists for that (--per-channel flag, _apply_per_channel in extract_graph.py, conv2d_s8_pc/linear_s8_pc with a curated RVV kernel: kernels/rvv/rvv_conv2d_s8_pc_direct.c) EXCEPT for gemmini/gemmini_q31, which has NO _pc curated kernel -- flipping --per-channel today would silently regress every gemmini conv2d_s8/linear_s8 from RoCC-accelerated to scalar-C reference. Scoped, not landed (not needed): a gemmini_q31 conv2d_s8_pc kernel is the prerequisite before --per-channel could ever be turned on for that backend.

change: ROOT CAUSE FOUND for BUG-rvv-f16-broken: NOT a kernel numerics bug -- a global conv weight-layout mismatch introduced by pipeline/reference_kernels.py's uncommitted target_affinity edit.
note: Isolated by host-recompiling reference_kernels.py's conv2d_f16/relu_f16/linear_f16/lstm_f16/cat3_c1_f16 reference C via ctypes and replaying the exact fused_full forward pass (real weights.npz + real sample input) op-by-op against PyTorch fp16 intermediates -- EVERY op matched PyTorch to fp16 rounding noise (<1e-3), including the final head output. So reference_kernels.py's C bodies are correct and the golden (io.npz) is correct (independently confirmed: PyTorch model.half()(*inputs.half()) reproduces io.npz's output bit-for-bit). Yet the ACTUAL on-device (spike) build of the SAME reference-only kernels.c produced a wildly different output (max_abs_err=0.376). Added temporary printf instrumentation to model.c's dispatch loop (disk-only, regenerated away by the next generate_skeleton run) and found vision_cnn.0's on-device conv2d_f16 output already diverges from the correct value at the FIRST op. Traced further: examples/fused_full/fp16/generated/rvv/weights.c's vision_cnn.0.weight literal values do NOT match weights.npz's OIHW layout element-for-element beyond index 0 -- they exactly match weights.npz TRANSPOSED to IHWOC (perm (1,2,3,0), verified numerically to full precision). Cause: pipeline/generate_skeleton.py::_conv_weight_layout_for_backend() derives ONE weight-layout decision for an ENTIRE backend by scanning ONLY CONV2D_S8's algorithms (not the op actually being packed), and _backend_pack_weight() applies that layout to EVERY 4D weight tensor in the model regardless of which op consumes it. Today's uncommitted reference_kernels.py diff added 'rvv_f16' to the target_affinity of conv2d_s8's THREE ihwoc-layout algorithms (rvv_widening_oc, rvv_vsmul_vnclip, rvv_oc_blocked) -- previously only 'rvv'. The 'near-uniform 0.374/0.375 error across every curated kernel' signature in BUG-rvv-f16-broken is explained: ALL of generate_kernels' curated-swap verify calls rebuild the FULL model against the same corrupted weights.c, so every op's isolated verify inherits the SAME upstream vision_cnn.0 corruption regardless of which op or algorithm is actually under test.

change: USER DIRECTION: fusion is a flagged optimization; replace binary accuracy labels with computed bounds
note: THREE DECISIONS. (1) conv+relu+pool fusion approved as an OPT-IN optimization behind an enable/disable flag, built on the EXISTING fusion pass infrastructure rather than a parallel mechanism -- note those passes currently fire zero times on yolov8n only because they key on ReLU while that model uses SiLU, so the machinery exists and simply is not matching. This removes the need for a global exact-vs-fast decision: both configurations stay available and measurable. (2) REPLACE the binary bit_exact/numeric_drift label with a QUANTIFIED per-layer bound. The tiled_conv drift is analytically characterised -- pre-rounding the SCALE rather than the PRODUCT converts a bounded +-0.5-output-unit error into one proportional to the accumulator, err ~= acc * delta where delta = round(mult,shift) - mult/2^shift. mult and shift are compile-time constants and the accumulator range is bounded by calibration, so a per-layer worst-case bound is computable STATICALLY. Motivation: accuracy_class is a claim, and two kernels claimed bit_exact while measuring err=17 in isolation; a computed bound can be checked, a label can only be trusted. (3) COST DECOMPOSITION with a likely free win: the exact path costs ~6.2x (11,598,513 vs 1,860,175 on dronet) from 4x drain traffic (int32 not int8; conv0 moves 401,408 B vs 100,352 B) PLUS a CPU requantize pass that re-reads it. On the PURE target that requantize is SCALAR -- gemmini_conv2d_s8_gemmini_im2col_full_C.c has ZERO __riscv_v intrinsics because vectorising would break purity. On the FUSED gemmini_q31_rvv target the same requantize can be vectorised while keeping the exact two-stage formula, recovering much of the gap with NO numeric change. Asked the agent to split the 6.2x into irreducible drain traffic versus recoverable scalar requantize; if favourable, exact-and-fast is achievable and the fusion trade becomes far less pressing.

note: pipeline/reference_kernels.py's CONV2D_F16 KernelSpec explicitly mandates an fp32 accumulator ('to avoid catastrophic cancellation when summing many partial products -- same pattern as Tensor Cores and what torch.float16 conv2d does on CPU. A true narrow path (vfmacc.vv on e16 vectors throughout, accumulator itself fp16, real reachable ceiling 16 ops/cyc per the RTL's nTandemFMA=2 segments) would reduce every reduction chain -- up to IC*KH*KW=64*3*3=576 terms for this model's deepest conv -- to running fp16 sums, well past where fp16's ~3 decimal digits of precision tracks an fp32 reference within the 0.0009765625-class tolerance this campaign has established as normal. NOTE for future work: `vfwmacc.vf` (id2005, landed) already gets the per-instruction-count benefit of a fused widen-multiply-accumulate without touching the ceiling; the ceiling itself is an RTL fact (dLenB/8=2 tandem-FMA segments halve throughput once the accumulator widens to fp32), not a coding choice, so 16 ops/cyc is only reachable by abandoning the semantics contract, not by a smarter instruction sequence.

note: CUMULATIVE SPLIT across all 10 dronet conv layers: transpose=1,052,263 (12.3%), im2col_build=3,727,975 (43.4%), gemm+drain_wait=66,573 (0.78%), cpu_requantize=3,740,646 (43.6%); 4-bucket sum=8,587,457 (a per-op wrapper 'total' number is NOT reported here -- it is inflated by this experiment's own per-call printf UART cost, which sits after all 4 timing brackets close and never pollutes the 4 buckets themselves, but does pollute any naive wrapper-level total; discard that number, trust the 4 buckets). KEY FINDING, CONTRADICTS THE COORDINATOR'S '4x drain traffic' FRAMING: gemmini's own GEMM+DMA-drain-wait is under 1% of the real measured cost on spike -- essentially free. The exact path's cost is overwhelmingly TWO roughly-equal CPU-SCALAR loops: im2col gather (43.4%) and Q0.31 requantize (43.6%), plus a smaller third scalar loop, the input transpose (12.3%). All three are pure data-movement/arithmetic scalar loops with no gemmini/RoCC instructions in them, and all three use the exact same int64/int8 formula regardless of vectorization -- so ALL THREE, not just the requantize the coordinator singled out, are candidates for RVV vectorization on the fused gemmini_q31_rvv target with NO numeric change (same bit-exact result). CAVEAT: this is a SPIKE (functional simulator) measurement, not FPGA-timing-accurate -- spike's gemmini functional model may not reflect real Saturn-Gemmini DMA/GEMM latency, so the near-zero gemm_drain bucket should be treated as 'negligible relative to the two scalar loops on THIS simulator', not asserted as an FPGA-validated absolute number; the historically-logged FPGA aggregate for this same kernel (9,889,329 post-transpose-opt / 11,598,513 pre-opt, id 1200/1303) is the same order of magnitude as this spike measurement's 8,587,457, which is at least consistent. RECOMMENDATION: before committing to vectorizing only the requantize on gemmini_q31_rvv, budget for vectorizing im2col gather too (roughly equal payoff) -- a single RVV strided/segment load can plausibly replace the innermost per-channel copy in both the transpose and im2col loops, since both are the same access pattern (contiguous IC-length runs at a strided offset).

Both bit-exact on real hardware (max_abs_err=0, stamp+model-banner verified). Per-layer split by tap count: 3x3 layers (39/63) overwhelmingly favor tiled-direct -- igemm faster in only 2/39, and loses by 6-9x on the worst small-channel 'bottleneck' layers inside C2f blocks (e.g. l21.m0.cv1.conv: tiled-direct 6.6x faster; detect.cv3_2_0.conv: tiled-direct 8.8x faster). 1x1 layers (24/63) are a mixed bag by COUNT (igemm faster in 11/24) but include igemm's largest wins by cycle count (l0.conv 2.14x, l2.cv1.conv 2.92x, l2.cv2.conv 2.46x -- the big early/high-spatial-extent layers). NET: tiled-direct wins in aggregate cycles because the 3x3 losses (37 layers, most of the network) outweigh the 1x1 wins. MECHANISM (consistent with the campaign's own conv2d_f16 finding re: strided vlse16 weight loads at ~1elem/cycle being a real, spike-invisible memory bottleneck): iGEMM's indirection buffer requires up to KH*KW=9 separate scattered/strided pointer-gather loads per input-channel-group for a 3x3 tap, each a real DRAM/cache-latency-bound access that spike's functional cycle model does not charge for the way real hardware does; for 1x1 (KH=KW=1, no spatial gather at all) the indirection buffer degenerates to a single contiguous-ish access per channel group and the per-reduction-index overhead amortization iGEMM was designed for shows through cleanly. CONCLUSION: the coordinator's structural hypothesis (iGEMM eliminates the per-tap overhead that tiling can only amortize around) is FALSIFIED for the dominant 3x3 case on real hardware -- it trades a compute/overhead cost for a memory-latency cost that is worse on this SoC's real memory system, though it IS a clear win specifically for 1x1/pointwise convs. Recommend NOT replacing the current tiled-direct kernel as the general conv2d_s8 default; rvv_igemm could be curated as a SHAPE-CONDITIONAL algorithm (KH==1 && KW==1) if that's worth the selector complexity -- not pursued further here, reporting the negative to the coordinator as requested.

change: TESTED AND REFUTED a hypothesis for id 2215's iGEMM-loses-on-3x3 finding, prompted by a user challenge ('is this really structural, or is iGEMM just under-optimized vs. a thoroughly-tuned direct kernel -- xnnpack gets much better conv utilization'). Code inspection found a real, concrete candidate cause: iGEMM's hot loop is tap-outer/ic-inner, paying the full channel-stride jump (IH*IW) on every innermost iteration (IC*taps times), while the tiled-direct kernel's hot loop is ic-outer/kw-inner, paying that same jump only ~IC times (KW-fold fewer expensive non-local jumps for KH*KW>1). Built a reordered variant (ic-outer, tap-inner, address computed as aptr_buf[tap]+ic*astep_buf[tap] since astep is uniformly the channel stride) across all 3 pixel-tile tiers (MR=4/2/1), verified bit-exact on spike (kernel_picks.json confirmed), then FPGA-measured on the same 63-layer yolov8n workload (3rd fq submission this session, well within the 3-lane budget).
curated: conv2d_s8/rvv_igemm reordered variant (temporary, NOT committed -- reverted to the original after this test; git status confirmed clean)
note: REFUTED: the reordered (ic-outer) variant is 33% SLOWER than the original (tap-outer) iGEMM overall (0.671x), and slower on BOTH 3x3 (0.71x of original) AND 1x1 (0.56x of original -- this hurts worse, even though original iGEMM was near-parity with baseline there, 0.979x). So the loop-order/locality hypothesis, AS IMPLEMENTED, is wrong or at least dominated by a different cost: the reorder replaced a cheap register-resident pointer INCREMENT (p+=step, live across the whole ic loop for a fixed tap) with a per-access RECOMPUTE (base[tap]+ic*step[tap], requiring fresh loads of aptr_buf/astep_buf from the stack array plus a multiply, on every single (ic,tap) inner iteration). That overhead evidently swamps whatever locality benefit the reordering was meant to capture. CONCLUSION: two good-faith implementations of iGEMM (original tap-outer/increment, and ic-outer/recompute) both lose to tiled-direct on 3x3 int8 conv on this hardware -- id 2215's negative result stands, but is NOT yet proven to be an inherent limit of the indirection-buffer concept itself, since a third design (ic-outer with genuinely register-resident incremental pointers, avoiding both the original's per-tap non-local jump AND this attempt's recompute overhead -- closer to what XNNPACK's hand-scheduled assembly microkernels actually do) was not attempted; that would require careful register-pressure-aware design (up to MR*taps=36 live pointers for 3x3, exceeding available GPRs, so spilling is a real risk there too) beyond what a straightforward intrinsics-loop reorder can guarantee. Recommending against further speculative iteration here without a more deliberate microkernel redesign -- reporting the refutation to the user/coordinator instead of continuing to guess.

change: Falsification attempt on the iGEMM loss: reorder iGEMM's hot loop to ic-outer/tap-inner
note: The iGEMM loss was challenged rather than accepted, and the challenge FAILED on hardware -- which strengthens the original negative. First, ruled out the obvious confound: both kernels already carry the SAME tiling stack (L1D output-channel cache blocking + 4->2->1 pixel register tiling), so this was never 'polished direct vs bare iGEMM'. Then a real structural difference was identified: the direct kernel's innermost loop runs over kw at fixed ic (a few contiguous bytes, one cache line), while iGEMM's runs over ic at a fixed tap, jumping the full IH*IW channel stride every iteration and taps-many times more often than necessary when KH*KW>1. That predicts exactly the observed pattern -- iGEMM clean-wins at 1x1 where the distinction vanishes, loses at 3x3 where it does not. The fix was built and FPGA-tested (bit-exact on spike first): reordering to ic-outer/tap-inner across all three pixel-tile tiers made it WORSE, 33% slower overall, and worse on BOTH shapes (3x3 0.71x, 1x1 0.56x -- it damaged even the case that had been near parity). Cause: the reorder swaps a register-resident pointer increment for a per-access recompute (fresh stack loads plus a multiply), and that overhead swamps the locality gain. Reverted, nothing committed. HONEST BOUND on the conclusion: two good-faith iGEMM implementations now lose to tiled-direct on 3x3 int8 conv on this hardware, and the result survived a direct attempt to falsify it -- but this does NOT prove iGEMM is inherently incapable here. A true XNNPACK-style microkernel keeps all tap pointers register-resident, which at 3x3 with 4-pixel tiling means up to 36 live pointers (4 pixels x 9 taps), likely exceeding available GPRs. A naive C-intrinsics reorder cannot replicate that; it needs deliberate register-pressure-aware design, which is a materially larger effort than what was attempted.

change: Investigated (and did NOT confirm) a GCC-clone codegen idiom as the cause of the dispatch's hardware-only numeric divergence.
note: Recorded because it is a real, reproducible codegen observation even though it turned out not to be the (only) culprit. Because the dispatch condition proves KH==KW==1, GCC clones the iGEMM as mb_conv2d_s8_igemm.constprop.0 with taps folded to 1. In the clone -- and in NO other build of this file, and not in the standalone kernels/rvv/rvv_conv2d_s8_rvv_igemm.c -- the three bias loads are scheduled as `vsetvli zero,zero,e8,m1,ta,ma; vle32.v v4,(t1)`, i.e. EEW=32 under SEW=8 so EMUL=4 is implied by the load's encoding. That is architecturally legal (vl and VLMAX agree, v4 is EMUL-aligned) and spike executes it correctly. Blocking the clone with __attribute__((noipa)) removes all three sites, and the noipa build is the one that ships. It did NOT fix the numerics: err went 6 -> 5, not 6 -> 0 (jobs 189/190 vs 193), and it costs ~3% of the pointwise win (2.1175x -> 2.0553x). So the mixed-EEW load is at most a contributing factor. Keeping noipa anyway: it restores the codegen of the standalone kernel that this file forked, which is the only iGEMM codegen that has ever measured err=0 on this FPGA, and 3% is cheap insurance. Flagging the idiom for whoever audits the Saturn RTL -- if mixed-EEW unit-stride loads are mishandled, this is another spike-invisible hazard of the same family as the conv2d_f16 strided vlse16 finding.

change: OBJ1 BISECT 2+3, BYTE-IDENTICAL-LAYOUT BINARY PATCHES of the crashing job-11 ELF. Because this defect is layout-sensitive, the bisect was done by patching TWO BYTES of the archived binary (a function's first instruction -> `ret`, c.jr ra = 0x8082) rather than rebuilding: every other byte, every symbol address, every buffer address and the whole .text/.rodata/.bss layout stay identical, so the only variable is whether that function's body executes. P1 (fq job 214) neutralises kernel_batchnorm2d_s8_yolov8_nano @0x800098c0. P2 (fq job 215) neutralises sp_tiled_conv.constprop.0 @0x80009326 -- the function that issues EVERY gemmini mvin/mvout/compute RoCC instruction inside tiled_conv_auto, i.e. it removes all Gemmini DMA and accelerator activity while leaving the conv kernel's transposes, workspaces and control flow intact.
note: P2 KILLS THE LEADING HYPOTHESIS. With ALL Gemmini activity removed the fault STILL happens, at the SAME instruction: mcause=1 mtval=0 mepc=0, ra=0x8000c066, sp=0x808fd9b0, mstatus=8000000a0001f880 -- byte-identical control state to the unpatched crash. So the Gemmini mvout-DMA race that this very conv kernel's header blames for 'mcause=1, mepc=0' is NOT the mechanism here. What DID change in P2 is which invocation dies: t0=t1=t3=0x1900=6400 and a0/a1=0x8060a6e0/0x80608de0 instead of 0xc800/buf_l2_cv1_act, i.e. a DIFFERENT, later silu call -- so the fault is bound to the CODE SITE, not to a dispatch, a buffer or a data value. P1 (batchnorm neutralised) runs to completion: 204 dispatches, 144,361,001 cycles, no fault (max_abs_err=84 is expected -- batchnorm is a no-op, the output is meant to be wrong). CONFOUND, STATED HONESTLY: P1 does not merely delete batchnorm, it also makes silu's input all-zero (the un-written bn output buffer), which sends every expf call down the same trivial path -- silu drops 232M -> 86.7M cycles. So P1 shows 'the fault needs batchnorm to run OR needs silu to see non-trivial inputs'; it does not by itself prove batchnorm is the corrupter. Note also that kernel_batchnorm2d_s8's reference impl is provably in-bounds (idx = ((n*C+c)*H+h)*W+w, max 102399 into a 102400-byte buffer, all int, no wrap), so it is not an out-of-bounds writer.

change: OBJ1 BISECT 4: P3, same 2-byte technique, neutralises kernel_silu_s8_yolov8_nano @0x8000bffa -> ret. Motivation: kernel_batchnorm2d_s8 contains the IDENTICAL code idiom the fault lands on -- `fdiv.s fa0,fa0,fs3; auipc ra,0x9; jalr -366(ra) -> roundf` at 0x800099f0..0x800099f8 (return address 0x800099fc) -- so if the fault were a property of that idiom alone it should relocate into batchnorm. fq job 216.
note: NO CRASH, AND IT DOES NOT RELOCATE. 204 dispatches complete with batchnorm running at full cost (e.g. l2.cv1.bn 4,098,307 cycles, l8.m0.cv2.bn 276,007) and silu a 20-cycle no-op; no fault at batchnorm's own roundf call site. So the `fdiv.s -> auipc ra -> jalr ra -> roundf` idiom is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT: something specific to silu's instance of it is required. The difference between the two instances is that silu reaches it through expf and TWO dependent back-to-back fdiv.s (0x8000c056 fdiv.s fa0,fs0,fa0 then 0x8000c05a fdiv.s fa0,fa0,fs2) whereas batchnorm has a single fdiv.s preceded by fcvt/fmul/fmadd, and that silu's auipc at 0x8000c05e straddles a 16-byte fetch boundary. MINIMAL RECIPE SO FAR: batchnorm2d_s8 must run AND silu_s8 must run; Gemmini need not.

change: OBJ1 ROOT CAUSE, BISECT 5: P4 changes TWO OPCODES and nothing else in the crashing job-11 ELF -- silu's two dependent back-to-back FP divides immediately before the faulting call, `fdiv.s fa0,fs0,fa0` @0x8000c056 (18a47553) and `fdiv.s fa0,fa0,fs2` @0x8000c05a (19257553), become `fmul.s` (10a47553 / 11257553). Same instruction length, same source and destination registers, same encoding slot, so every byte of layout, every symbol address and the auipc/jalr pair that follows are bit-identical. The ONLY variable is the FPU operation class, i.e. whether a long-latency non-pipelined divide is in flight when the call retires. fq job 218.
note: THE FAULT DISAPPEARS. Runs past the crash point (which was dispatch 8) all the way to MODELBLASTER_VERIFY. max_abs_err=170 is expected and irrelevant -- the arithmetic was deliberately changed; the experiment is about the fault, not the numerics. THIS CLOSES THE BISECT. One predicate explains ALL SIX runs of this binary: 'silu's two dependent FULL-LATENCY fdiv.s execute immediately before the auipc+jalr to roundf'. TRUE -> faults: unpatched on 20MHz (job 11 and 213) and on 60MHz (job 212); P2 with all Gemmini activity removed (job 215). FALSE -> completes: P1 (job 214, batchnorm neutralised, which leaves silu's input all-zero so both divides have a zero numerator and Rocket's divider early-outs); P3 (job 216, silu not executed at all); P4 (job 218, divides replaced by multiplies). Note P2 is the control that rules out 'any data perturbation fixes it': P2 changes silu's input data drastically (all conv outputs become zero) and the fault SURVIVES, moving to a different silu invocation (n=6400) at the SAME instruction. So it is the divide latency, not the data. VERDICT: this is NOT a ModelBlaster kernel defect. Nothing in the software path is out of bounds (batchnorm's idx maxes at 102399 into a 102400 buffer; silu is a flat loop; the dispatch table is provably intact, log id 3001), and a pc-relative auipc+jalr to a link-time-constant target CANNOT transfer to 0 in any correct execution. It is a core-level control-transfer/fetch failure on the Rocket+Saturn+Gemmini F2 bitstream, triggered by a specific FP-divide-in-flight vs auipc+jalr alignment, which is exactly why it is invisible to spike, why it moved between builds, and why it survived every software-level theory the campaign tried.

change: First measurement of fused_full on Gemmini: the cost of a single-datatype accelerator on a mixed-precision net
note: gemmini_q31 (pure) = 295,276,993 cycles, max_abs_err=0, ELF name + model banner verified in the uartlog, kernel_picks.json read. THE SPLIT IS THE FINDING: 98.46% of the model (290,716,117 cycles) is the fp16 tail Gemmini structurally cannot touch, and the single op it accelerates is 1.54%. Per op: lstm_f16 x3 203,186,573 (68.81%); linear_f16 x3 87,360,860 (29.59%); conv2d_s8 x6 4,560,876 (1.54%); cast_i8_to_f16 x3 165,939; cat3_c1_f16 2,745. MECHANISM VERIFIED IN THE ELF, not inferred: -march=rv64imafdc carries no Zfh, so __extendhfsf2/__truncsfhf2 are linked and kernel_linear_f16's innermost K-reduction loop is literally 'lh; fmv.w.x; call __extendhfsf2; fmadd.s' -- ONE LIBGCC CALL PER MAC. SECONDARY, gemmini_q31_rvv = 294,586,452 max_abs_err=0, recovering only 0.23%: kernels/gemmini_q31_rvv/ has six curated kernels and not one is fp16, and they cannot be ported because that target's -march=rv64imafdcv adds V but still no Zfh/Zvfh, which the rvv_f16 kernels require; kernel_linear_f16 in that ELF contains ZERO vector instructions. Only conv2d_s8 moves (3.02x) and at 1.5% of the model that buys 1%, while lstm_f16 goes 1.16% the WRONG way (hart-1 pinning + eager V context). Against the curated RVV fused_full baseline of 4,922,762: 60.0x and 59.8x SLOWER. This is a genuine architectural outcome, not a measurement artifact -- it quantifies what a mixed-precision network costs on an accelerator that supports exactly one data type.

TWO FURTHER BUGS FOUND: (1) the existing _check_conv_family_layout_agreement trip-wire could not catch this -- it compares DECLARED layouts between specs and was handed s8_layout='oihw', which agrees with conv2d_f16's 'oihw'; it cannot see that a curated FILE exists for an algorithm not affined to that target, because the curated probe discovers files by path and never consults target_affinity. (2) LATENT, and the one I had independently flagged earlier as the likely cause of the all-reference err=92: the universal reference used a single index expression for both packings, but hwio=(H,W,I,O) and ihwoc=(I,H,W,O) are different permutations, so 64/72 elements read from the wrong offset. Harmless while curated kernels always win, but enabling ihwoc on rvv_f16 would have converted the SAFE fallback into a silently WRONG one. Negative control: reverting that hunk alone fails a pure-reference build at 0.201. FIX (4 files): rvv_f16 added to the four ihwoc algorithms; RVV_F16 gains -DMODELBLASTER_RVV_IHWOC_WEIGHTS=1; weight packing resolved PER OP rather than per backend (required, since conv2d_s8 wants ihwoc and conv2d_f16 wants oihw on the same backend); if/elif split at 4 sites for the HWIO/IHWOC bug. No tolerance loosened, nothing relabeled, no kernel deleted. PROOF OF SELECTION, not just of correctness: build log '[conv2d_s8/rvv_vsmul_vnclip] curated verify PASS max_abs_err=0.000183' and kernel_picks.json source=curated algorithm=rvv_vsmul_vnclip (was source=reference algorithm=null); weights.c now has 6 repack comments. Collateral fix: cast_i8_to_f16 also went FAIL(0.19)->PASS, having only failed because the curated pre-seed put the broken conv kernel in its verify baseline. FPGA: conv2d_s8 163,023,800 -> 2,851,311 (57.2x), model 165,164,353 -> 4,956,577 (33.3x), max_abs_err 0.00048828125. RESTORATION, NOT OPTIMIZATION: against the same curated kernel's recorded best of 2,842,309 this is +0.32%, i.e. noise. Blast radius A/B of emit_weights, HEAD vs fixed, 4 models x 4 backends: byte-identical on 13/16, the 3 differing cells being exactly rvv_f16 with 4D conv weights. NEW GUARD _assert_curated_layout_contract() at all three curated-discovery sites refuses a curated file whose algorithm's weight_layout differs from what the skeleton packs for that op on that target; swept all 55 curated kernels, 0 violations post-fix, fires with an actionable message pre-fix. change: TACIT basic-block tracing on AWS F2: capture works, the byte stream is corrupt -- no analysis possible
note: CLEAN NEGATIVE, root-caused with a control experiment. The requested per-basic-block attribution was NOT produced, and the reason is a data-integrity failure in the F2 trace path, not a tooling or usage error. WHAT WORKS: the trace hardware is live on F2 -- the guest reads TR_TE_CTRL back as 0x1 -> 0x3 (start) -> 0x1 (stop) around model_run_test(), and bytes do reach the host as tacit0.out/tacit1.out per tile in /home/ubuntu/sim_slot_0/. The traced build itself is sound: max_abs_err=0, full profile table, 7,539,118 summed op cycles, all 7 ops on curated kernels per kernel_picks.json. WHAT IS BROKEN: (1) the bridge injects 4-byte zero blocks -- U250 reference has 3 zero bytes in 3,000,000 (0.00%); F2 run 1 has 473 zero bytes in 92 runs of EXACTLY 4; F2 run 2 is 98.77% zeros in one 2,963,184-byte run; F2 run 3 is 25,317,376 bytes and 100% zeros, with tile 0 streaming only zeros while tile 1 on the same run carried a real sync packet. Quantised 32-bit lane-fill, not random loss. (2) The sync packet's address is truncated reproducibly -- it carries the only absolute PC in a TACIT trace and everything after is a delta; 5 varint bytes are expected and 3 arrive, across 3 runs / 2 harts / 2 hosts / 2 ELFs, with the low 21 bits always matching the ELF exactly (0x8000056a = the sw that enables the encoder) and the top two groups plus terminator gone, yielding a garbage PC of 0x1ec0056a. (3) Even with the start PC pinned via a new TACIT_START_PC override, decode dies within 1-2 packets at a jalr with no FUj packet -- only 7 0x0a bytes in the whole model trace against at least 21 kernel returns. INTEGRITY CONTROL that makes this trustworthy: the U250 reference sums to 216,597,098 cycle-deltas against 216,597,443 expected = 100.0%, with zero framing breaks in 72,173,559 packets; the F2 model trace has 46 breaks in 59.5 KB. RULED OUT: the decoder (the same binary decodes U250 correctly); and TacitEncoder.scala, TraceSinkRawByte.scala, TacitModule.scala, TacitBridge.scala, tacit.cc, rocket-chip trace/* and RocketCore.scala are all md5-IDENTICAL between garden's tree and the AWS tree that built the F2 bitstream, despite different rocket-chip commits and tacit branches. Also ruled out: branch-predictor mode, all three guest enable sequences, start-of-stream byte drops. LEADING FIX (untested): gate the bridge on valid/mask -- TraceSinkRawByte drives out.mask(0) := io.trace_in.valid and out.valid := io.trace_in.valid, so check whether the F2 TacitBridge/StreamToHostCPU path honours them instead of streaming zero-filled beats; the 4-byte quantisation points at 32-bit lanes. That is an RTL change requiring an F2 bitstream rebuild. TWO LESSONS BEYOND THIS TASK: (a) the corruption is SILENT -- 0x00 is a legal 1-byte TACIT packet, so a 100%-zero file parses as an endless run of valid packets, and the agent's own first framing metric called run 2 'clean' when it was 98.8% zeros; use the timestamp-sum check instead. (b) trace bandwidth throttles the simulation -- sink egress is 1 lane / 1 byte per beat (~50 KB/s observed), and with boot tracing on the guest never reached main in 15 minutes because tracing throttles the target, starving HTIF, whose spin loop retires more branches and produces more trace. Widen the egress before reviving this. ALSO FOUND: fq does NOT collect the trace -- fq/backends/firesim.py hardcodes common_simulation_outputs: ['uartlog'], so trace files must be scp'd off the run host; helper saved as experiments/tacit/f2_tacit_run.sh. change: FIXED a shape bug in extract_graph_export._emit_linear that inflated M and overran output buffers
note: BUG: M was computed as prod(in_shape[:-1]). Aliases (flatten/view/reshape) are zero-cost, so _resolve_input returns the PRE-reshape producer whose trailing dim is not in_features. Three sites in ViNT: goal-encoder `linear` read the 4D pooled (1,1280,1,1) -> M=1280 (true 1), the four attention out-projections read (1,4,7,128) -> M=28 (true 7), and linear_18 read (1,7,512) -> M=1 vs emitted 7. Consequences were not subtle: dispatch 295 emitted kernel_linear_f16(..., M=1280, K=1280, N=512) writing 655,360 halves into buf_vint_linear[512] -- a 1.3 MB overrun -- and 1280x the arithmetic, 839 MMAC of pure garbage that would have swamped the whole 360 MMAC model. FIX: M = numel(in)/in_features with a fallback to the old rule when it does not divide. Verified post-fix: every linear now satisfies M*N == numel(output). Blast radius is only the torch.export ingest path (--model choices are vint and smolvla); the FX extractor other models use is untouched.

change: FOUND (not fixed): the export path does not implement multi-head attention -- Q, K and V collapse to one buffer and 3 of 4 heads are never computed
note: _emit_scaled_dot_product_attention takes only the LAST TWO dims of q/k/v, so a (1,4,7,128) tensor becomes a single (7,128) matmul: scores are emitted as [7,7] not [4,7,7], and the av matmul writes 896 of the 3584 elements its output tensor declares. Worse, the generated call is kernel_matmul_s8(buf_linear_2, buf_linear_2, ...) -- the SAME base pointer for Q, K and V, with no head or qkv-slice offset -- so it computes Q0.Q0^T and never reads K or V at all. Same root cause as vint-002: zero-cost alias resolution discards the slice/transpose that distinguishes q, k and v inside the fused qkv projection. IMPACT ON THIS TASK IS SMALL AND BOUNDED: the 8 matmul_s8 + 4 softmax_s8 ops are 0.05 MMAC and 0.05% of measured cycles, so the performance characterisation stands; what is invalid is end-to-end accuracy. Spike end-to-end vs the fp32 golden is max_abs_err=0.3279 / max_rel_err=0.1460 on the 21-value output, and that number must NOT be read as ViNT's quantisation error. Fixing it needs a batched matmul (B=4) in the matmul_s8/softmax_s8 ABI plus per-head qkv slicing in the walker -- deliberately not attempted here because reference_kernels.py is being edited concurrently.

change: Re-derived Gemmini's Q0.31 ACC_SCALE unit from RTL + generated header and PROVED by exhaustive search that a single HW mvout requantize can never be bit-exact against modelblaster's two-stage (CMSIS-NN) golden for output_shift>0
note: GROUND TRUTH. (a) RTL and header AGREE: Q31Configs.scala's scale lambda is `prod = t*m; biased = prod +& (1.S<<30); shifted = (biased >> 31)` -- shift by 31, matching gemmini_params.h's ACC_SCALE macro exactly; soc/sim/gemmini_models/q31ws_16x16/gemmini_params.h is a ZERO-LINE diff against modelblaster/cores/gemmini/include/gemmini_params.h. The unit is EXACT INTEGER arithmetic -- it is NOT 'inherently lossy', there is no float anywhere, and mvin scale left at MVIN_SCALE_IDENTITY is genuinely inert. (b) ACC_SCALE_IDENTITY = (1<<30) is 0.5, NOT 1.0: ACC_SCALE(100, 1<<30) == 50. Verified. The true exact identity for this format is 0x7FFFFFFF: ACC_SCALE(x, 0x7FFFFFFF) == x for every x in [-2^20, 2^20) (checked exhaustively; holds analytically to |x| <= 2^30). acc_scale_identity is HEADER-ONLY (GemminiConfigs.scala:419, no RTL use), so fixing the constant needs NO bitstream rebuild -- but it WOULD break gemmini_q31_maxpool2d_s8_gemmini_tiled_conv_pool.c, which deliberately compensates for the halving with weight=+2. (c) THE KEY IDENTITY: the golden's two-stage round is algebraically a ONE-stage round with a bigger numerator bias -- floor((floor((acc*M + 2^30)/2^31) + 2^(s-1))/2^s) == floor((acc*M + 2^30 + 2^(30+s))/2^(31+s)) exactly (verified on 200,000 random (M,s,acc) triples, 0 mismatches). The HW gives floor((acc*m + 2^30)/2^31): with m = M/2^s the shift matches but the numerator is short by exactly 2^(30-s). That deficit is acc-INDEPENDENT, so the ONLY lever is the accumulator bias (bias += beta contributes beta*m); the required beta is 2^(30-s)/m = 2^30/M, which lies in (0.5, 1] and is therefore NEVER an integer except at M == 2^30. beta=1 is provably the best integer choice. (d) EXHAUSTIVE PROOF, not an estimate: for each of dronet's 10 conv layers I enumerated EVERY int32 accumulator value that can produce an in-range int8 output (57k-446k values per layer) against 65 multipliers x 17 bias offsets. Minimum mismatch count is STRICTLY POSITIVE for all 10 layers (13, 1, 121, 75, 4, 122, 35, 47, 41, 102), and matches the closed form 255*(1 - 2^30/M). CONCLUSION: tiled_conv_auto cannot be bit-exact on this datapath -- the campaign's verdict stands -- but the REASON in the kernel headers is wrong. It is not 'float scale', not 'lossy ACC_SCALE', and not 'pre-rounding the scale scales the error with acc' (that term is ~1e-4 LSB and irrelevant); it is a hardwired rounding bias of 2^30 at a hardwired shift of 31, one representable-constant short of the golden. Script: scratchpad q31_proof.py / q31_wide.py; layer params from examples/*/int8/generated/graph.json.

change: Bit-exact HARDWARE im2col: Gemmini's mvin DMA does the patch gather (strided/overlapping reads of a zero-padded NHWC activation), KH chained int32 matmuls accumulate through full_C partials, exact two-stage Q0.31 requantize stays on the CPU
curated: 7/7 (add_s8, conv2d_s8, linear_s8, maxpool2d_s8 curated; rest reference)
note: THE CAMPAIGN'S PREMISE WAS WRONG, AND THIS FIXES IT. Bit-exactness never required doing im2col in software -- it required draining int32 instead of int8. Those are separable. For a fixed kernel row kh, A[p][kw*IC+ic] = padded_nhwc[n, oh*SH+kh, ow*SW+kw, ic] is an AFFINE 2-D DRAM pattern: row stride = SW*IC, and the (kw,ic) column index spans KW*IC CONTIGUOUS bytes because the activation is NHWC. That is precisely config_ld + mvin, so tiled_matmul_auto reads the im2col patch matrix -- overlapping rows and all -- directly out of the activation with stride_A=SW*IC, dim_K=KW*IC. The KH kernel rows chain through int32 partials (kh=0: D=bias, C=P0; kh=1: D=P0, C=P1; ...) with full_C=true and low_D=false; MVIN_SCALE_ACC is a hardwired no-op on this config, so the accelerator never rounds and the acc-scale unit is never touched. Zero padding is materialised once, fused into the NCHW->NHWC transpose the kernel already had to do. Result: ws_im2col and the entire scalar gather loop are GONE. MEASURED, REAL FPGA, f2_dual_small_norose_tacit_q31_60mhz, provenance-verified (fq job 241 prog0=fq-job-2410-hwc_base.elf vs job 242 prog0=fq-job-2420-hwc_A.elf, same harness banner model=dronet in=37632 out=2, same IR): conv2d_s8 9,757,075 -> 6,415,770 cycles (1.521x), whole model 14,147,329 -> 10,811,936 (1.308x), MODELBLASTER_VERIFY max_abs_err=0 on BOTH. Spike curated-verify max_abs_err=0 max_rel_err=0 at all 15 dronet conv shapes with MAX_ACCURACY_CLASS=bit_exact (atol 0.0), and at all 45 yolov8_nano conv shapes. Baseline is the CURATED gemmini_im2col_full_C, not the scalar reference. Per-layer (base -> new, speedup): conv0 6,989,156->3,852,395 1.81x; conv1 673,936->673,306 1.00x; conv2 520,618->317,639 1.64x; conv3 490,135->580,615 0.84x; conv4 242,144->198,054 1.22x; conv5 240,469->185,647 1.30x; conv6 185,690->158,652 1.17x; conv7 143,299->155,431 0.92x; conv8 160,929->189,866 0.85x; conv9 110,699->104,165 1.06x. The three regressions are all small-OW layers and have ONE cause: each (oh, kh) is a separate tiled_matmul_auto call, so the B (weight) matrix is re-mvin'd every call. conv8 moves 12 x 49,152 = 590 KB of weight vs the baseline's single 147 KB -- 4x the weight traffic to save 18 KB of gather. Fix (not done here): drive sp_tiled_matmul_ws directly and hold B resident across the oh loop via b_spad_id, which tiled_matmul_auto does not expose. Kernel staged, NOT landed, at experiments_hwc/kernels_A/gemmini_q31/gemmini_q31_conv2d_s8_gemmini_im2col_full_C.c (pure scalar, no vector instructions -- eligible for kernels/gemmini_q31/). Deliberately not landed in the shared kernels/ tree while other agents are mid-A/B against it.

change: Zero only the halo of the padded NHWC workspace instead of memsetting the whole buffer (the interior is fully overwritten by the transpose anyway)
note: HARDWARE-REFUTED spike win -- logged as the negative it is. On dronet the full memset is up to 38 KB/layer (yolov8 l1: 112 KB) of pure redundant stores, and removing it looked like a clear win on spike: conv2d_s8 5,736,772 -> 5,180,000 (1.107x), still max_abs_err=0. On REAL FPGA it is a small REGRESSION: 6,415,770 -> 6,548,810 (0.980x), whole model 10,811,936 -> 11,035,644 (fq job 243, prog0=fq-job-2430-hwc_A2.elf, max_abs_err=0). Reason: the full memset is one long sequential streaming write that the memory system absorbs cheaply, while the halo version replaces it with many short strided per-row border loops with worse locality and more loop overhead per byte. Spike counts instructions, so it scored the trade backwards. Keep the simple full zero-fill. Second data point (after the two ideas already refuted in the shipped kernel's header) that spike cycle counts do not rank memory-system changes on this SoC.
