change: Gate the DMA-gather path on KH*KW>1 (use the old CPU-im2col path for 1x1 convs, where there is no gather to hardware-ise) -- the obvious per-shape dispatch suggested by hwim2col-005's per-layer table
note: HARDWARE-REFUTED, AND THE REASON IS THE INTERESTING PART: PER-LAYER A/B NUMBERS ON THIS SoC DO NOT COMPOSE. Composing the measured per-layer minima predicted conv2d_s8 = 57,793,209 (1.213x) on yolov8_nano and 6,358,862 (1.534x) on dronet -- better than the ungated kernel on both. MEASURED (fq job 247 prog0=fq-job-2470-hwc_yA3.elf, job 246 prog0=fq-job-2460-hwc_A3.elf, both max_abs_err=0): yolov8_nano 63,692,078 (1.101x) and dronet 7,604,700 (1.283x) -- WORSE than the prediction AND worse than the ungated kernel (60,401,247 / 6,415,770). Decomposing by shape class nails it: in the gated binary the KH*KW>1 layers execute BYTE-IDENTICAL hardware-gather code, yet cost 40,376,259 vs the ungated binary's 34,595,574 -- 1.167x slower for the same instructions on the same data (dronet: 1.208x). The 1x1 layers, which run the baseline code, match the baseline binary to within 1.005x. Mechanism: the gated kernel keeps BOTH paths' static workspaces live -- ws_pad 256K + 2 x 64K partials for the DMA path PLUS ws_input 512K + ws_im2col 36K + ws_acc 16K for the CPU path, ~948 KB versus the ungated kernel's 384 KB -- and the two sets alternate through the model with zero reuse, so every 1x1 layer evicts the 3x3 layers' padded activation buffer. In the ungated kernel ws_pad is touched by every layer and stays warm. LESSON for this campaign: a per-shape dispatch rule fitted to per-layer A/B deltas is not safe to compose -- working-set effects across layer boundaries can exceed the per-layer deltas being optimised. Adopt the SIMPLE ungated kernel (experiments_hwc/kernels_A/), not the 'smarter' gated one (kernels_A3/, kept for the record).

change: FOUND AND FIXED an unguarded static-buffer overflow in the SHIPPED curated conv2d_s8_pc kernel
note: kernels/rvv_f16/rvv_f16_conv2d_s8_pc_direct.c stages the transposed weights in static int8 mb_wt[65536], the receptive-field patches in mb_patch[4*1024] and the drain in mb_drain[256]. Its own header comment says those were sized from ONE model -- 'This model's convs: max R=IC*KH*KW=576, max R*OC=36864, max OC=64' -- and NOTHING CHECKED IT. ViNT's EfficientNet-B0 blows through all of them: R=1152 (x1.1), R*OC=409,600 (x6.2), OC=1280 (x5.0), so the weight transpose `mb_wt[r*OC+oc]` writes up to index 1,474,559 into a 65,536-byte array. That is 1.4 MB of silent .bss corruption on every ViNT conv. HOW IT SURFACED, which is the interesting part: it is invisible until the .bss layout moves. Adding my new kernels' statics changed conv2d_s8_pc's measured cost 297.9M -> 342.3M with identical picks and identical source; then merely adding __attribute__((aligned(64))) to one 1 KB array and deleting one dead 4 KB array made the model produce WRONG output and conv2d_s8_pc jump to 9,226,403,956 cycles. Same kernel, same shapes, same picks -- only the neighbours moved. FIX (additive, no behaviour change for any in-bounds model): raise the caps to 1 MB / 8192 / 1024 AND add a hard capacity guard at kernel entry that falls back to a bit-exact scalar computation rather than scribbling past the buffers. After the fix the model output is bit-identical to the pre-fix reference-heavy baseline and max_abs_err is unchanged at 0.327884674, so the corruption was landing in dead .bss on spike -- but the same overflow exists in the FPGA build where the layout differs, and it is the leading candidate for the ViNT FPGA hang recorded in vint-006. THE IDENTICAL BUG IS STILL LIVE IN kernels/rvv/rvv_conv2d_s8_pc_direct.c (byte-identical twin, same caps, no guard) -- NOT patched here because dronet/yolov8/fused_full builds are running against it right now and they are all within the caps; whoever owns that file should take the same two-line guard.

change: Wrote 15 new curated rvv_f16 kernels (5 native-fp16, 10 int8/copy-shaped) and copied 11 existing int8 kernels across; 6 -> 24 of 30 op kinds curated
note: 1,609,508,008 -> 785,124,063 cycles = 2.05x on the whole model, with the scalar-reference share falling from 75.79% to 2.29%. CORRECTNESS IS DIFFERENTIAL AND EXACT: all 21 model outputs are BIT-IDENTICAL to the reference-heavy 6-curated baseline, so not one of the 18 newly-selected kernels changes a single output value at ViNT's real shapes. That test had to be built by hand because THE BUILT-IN CURATED VERIFY GATE CANNOT BE USED ON ViNT: it swaps in the candidate, runs the WHOLE model and compares against the io.npz golden, and ViNT already misses that golden by 0.328 for an unrelated reason (the SDPA head bug, vint-003), so the gate rejected every single curated kernel including ones already shipped -- 'curated verify FAIL - model output diverged from golden (max_abs_err=0.328)' for adaptive_avg_pool2d_f16 on its very first probe. A model with any pre-existing divergence cannot use the gate at all; the differential test (same golden, curated build vs reference build, require bit-identical) is the right instrument there and is strictly stronger for the question 'did my kernel change anything'. NEW FP16 KERNELS, native Zvfh, no int8 emulation and no gratuitous widening: mul_f16 (vfmul.vv at eew=16, LMUL=8 -- bit-exact because the exact product of two fp16 fits in fp32, so the reference's f32 path and a native fp16 multiply both round exactly once) 7.0M->0.13M = 53.8x; relu_f16 (vfmax.vf) 12,017->236 = 50.9x; mul_c1_f16 (vfmul.vf broadcast) 2.21M->0.22M = 10.3x; add_f16 (vfadd.vv) unchanged in cycles but now vectorised; sigmoid_f16 -- the interesting one -- replaces a per-element expf() with a vector exp (rint octave split, 2-part ln2 range reduction, degree-6 Horner, 2^n by f32 exponent injection, then one reciprocal), 52.5M->1.6M = 33.3x, declared numeric_drift honestly since a degree-6 Taylor is ~1e-7 relative against a libm expf; batchnorm2d_f16 is the ONE place widening is used and it is not a preference -- the reference deliberately computes s*x+b in f32 (its own comment records that pure-fp16 accumulation caused 30-50% drift through the EfficientNet body), so vfwmacc.vf keeps the product exact and rounds once, bit-identical, with fp16 loads/stores throughout: 7.86M->0.35M = 22.4x. NEW INT8 KERNELS: depthwise_conv2d_s8 459.6M->305.9M = 1.50x (vwadd+vwmacc over ow, scalar bit-exact requant drain modelled on the shipped conv kernel; deliberately NOT vsmul/vnclip, which this tree records as measuring err=3 on FPGA); mul_s8 167.2M->2.86M = 58.4x; mul_c1_s8 29.6M->2.26M = 13.1x; pad_s8 22.8M->2.66M = 8.6x; adaptive_avg_pool2d_s8 19.9M->10.8M = 1.83x (bit-exact: the window sum is int32 and therefore exact under reassociation, and the requant is one op per OUTPUT so it stays scalar); pad_f16 5.58M->0.49M = 11.3x; adaptive_avg_pool2d_f16 3.32M->; cat2_c1_f16 0.39M->5,913 = 66x; slice_c_f16 0.196M->3,116 = 63x. Also copied 11 int8 kernels that already existed on rvv into rvv_f16 (sigmoid_s8, add_s8, cat2/3/4_c1_s8, batchnorm2d_s8, linear_s8, maxpool2d_s8, relu_s8, silu_s8, upsample_nearest_s8) -- pure integer, so identical under the rvv_f16 -march superset; only the first three are exercised by ViNT, the rest are there for other models. WHAT IS LEFT: the model is now 43.8% conv2d_s8_pc (curated, 1.68 cyc/MAC) + 39.0% depthwise_conv2d_s8 (curated, 14.7 cyc/MAC) + 9.0% linear_s8_pc (curated, 0.75 cyc/MAC). depthwise is the one with headroom -- only 48.8% of its output elements take the vector path because the border columns and the SW=2 stages are peeled to scalar, and ViNT's late stages are 2x2 and 4x5 planes where OW is shorter than a vector. The fix is a C-major vectorisation (channels are the long axis there, 480-1152 of them) which needs strided vlse8, and this tree has a recorded Saturn vlse8 corruption -- so it needs an FPGA A/B, not a spike one. Remaining reference ops are only 2.29% total: gelu_s8 15.0M (1.91%, 261 cyc/elem, a LUT would make it free), layer_norm_s8 2.1M, matmul_s8 0.84M, softmax_s8 0.04M, cast_f16_to_i8, vint_action_post.

change: PROPOSAL (not implemented): curated-kernel fallback from a backend to an ISA-subset donor backend

Any model that auto-promotes rvv -> rvv_f16 -- ViNT and fused_full both do -- silently loses every rvv-only kernel and drops those ops to scalar reference. On ViNT that alone was 26.2% of runtime. PROPOSAL: add `curated_fallback: tuple[str, ...] = ()` to Backend in pipeline/backends.py, set RVV_F16.curated_fallback=('rvv',) and SCALAR_F16.curated_fallback=('scalar',), and at the three probe sites try the backend's own directory first and then each donor in order, using the DONOR's filename prefix for the donor's directory. change: FOUND: both shipped curated fp16 CONV kernels fault on FPGA at ViNT's shapes while running clean on spike
note: Once the conv2d_s8_pc buffer overflow (vint-008) was fixed, the ViNT FPGA run stopped hanging silently and started FAULTING IMMEDIATELY -- which is far more useful. A faulting address of 3 means a computed base of ~0, not a plausible tensor address. (2) fq job 249, same build with oc_blocked removed so the picker fell to conv2d_f16/widening: 'mcause: 5, Load access fault, mtval: 0x7aa61300c', mepc=0x80019452 = kernel_depthwise_conv2d_f16_vint = rvv_f16_depthwise_conv2d_f16_oc_vec.c -- 0x7aa61300c is outside the 0x80000000 DRAM window entirely. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: the fp16 conv family cannot be measured on F2 at ViNT's shapes until those two kernels are debugged on hardware; they are only 2.26% + 0.42% of the model, so job 250 was submitted with both dropped to reference and the other 22 curated kernels (including all 15 new ones) intact. ALSO WORTH NOTING FOR THE HANG STORY: before the overflow fix the same model ran 90 minutes on FPGA with no fault and no output; after it, the same shapes trap in seconds. ViNT's 22-curated build is ~0.8-2.4 G spike cycles depending on how the two dropped fp16 convs are counted, so the expected FPGA cost is tens of seconds at 60 MHz, and 3600 s is at least two orders of magnitude past it. RULED OUT ACROSS THESE FIVE RUNS: the conv2d_s8_pc .bss overflow (fixed in vint-008, run 250 is memory-safe); the two faulting fp16 conv kernels (dropped in run 250); wrong backend (CMakeCache MODELBLASTER_BACKEND=rvv_f16, -march=rv64gcv_zfh_zvfh, rvv_f16.conf applied so CONFIG_RISCV_ISA_EXT_V=y and CONFIG_FPU=y); memory exhaustion (52.5 MB of a 256 MB region, link clean); MMU/TLB effects (no CONFIG_MMU on this board); kernel stack overflow (largest kernel local in the whole generated TU is int8_t lut[256]). STILL OPEN and the two candidates I would chase next: something that scales with image or working-set size on this bitstream -- ViNT's 31 MB ELF and 60 MB working set are ~7x anything previously run on it, dronet is 0.9 MB and yolov8_nano 4.4 MB -- or a further Saturn-vs-spike divergence in one of the remaining 22 curated kernels that manifests as a livelock rather than a trap. The cheap next experiment is a bisect: build ViNT with N curated kernels and all-reference for the rest, N descending, and find the smallest set that still hangs; each run is a 40 s build.

question: impact of SHARDING DIMENSION (split degree k -> tile width w) on per-op cost
placement: all tiles serial on CPU_E#0 (isolates work conservation from concurrency tax)
metric: work_ratio = sum(tile times)/unsplit time; 1.0 = perfect split, k = full duplication. cost_P<n> = ceil(k/n)*tile_time, the makespan of packing k tiles onto n harts; this SoC gives P=2 per same-kind pair.

Confirms the 32-channel slab model at k=2,4,8: median |err| 0.045x over 9 cells.
Non-obvious prediction held: OC=128 stays ratio ~1.0 at BOTH k=2 (1.002) and k=4 (1.005), then jumps to 1.955 at k=8, because ceil((OC/k)/32) only increments once the tile drops below one slab.

ACTIONABLE: on a P-hart pair the optimal split degree is k=P. k>P is neutral at best (OC=128 k=4 = -49.8%, same as k=2) and catastrophic when it breaks slab granularity (OC=32 k=4 = +94%, k=8 = +287%).
P=4 column is hypothetical for a future SoC with 4 units of one kind: OC=128 k=4 would give -74.9%.
Largest miss is conv_modules.0 (1.679 vs 2.0 predicted): the IC=3 first layer, where the input is tiny relative to weights so the per-slab input sweep is not the dominant term.

question: Is split cost driven by ALIGNMENT (each tile width a whole multiple of the backend blocking quantum) rather than by EVENNESS (equal tiles)?
placement: every tile serial on one hart (work conservation, no concurrency tax)
metric: work_ratio = sum(tile times)/unsplit time; 1.0 = split is free
model: slab model: work_ratio = sum_i ceil(w_i/Q)/ceil(OC/Q); Q=32 rvv (vsetvlmax_e32m4 at VLEN=256), Q=16 gemmini (DIM)
notes: VERDICT 1 -- alignment beats evenness outright. At OC=128 on rvv the three aligned-and-EVEN cells (64,64) average work_ratio 1.0033 and the seven aligned-but-UNEVEN cells ((96,32),(32,96),(32,32,64)) average 1.0084; the six misaligned cells ((16,112),(32,48,48)) average 1.2423 = the predicted 5/4. Evenness moves the number by 0.5%, alignment by 24%.

VERDICT 2 -- (96,32) IS equivalent to (64,64). Per-operator: conv_modules.7 1.0024 vs 1.0011, conv_modules.8 1.0026 vs 1.0008, conv_modules.9 1.0104 vs 1.0080. Every difference is under the +-2.5% noise floor. The uneven-but-aligned partition is free.

VERDICT 3 -- the k=3 arm removes evenness as a variable entirely: 128 is not divisible by 3, so NO even 3-way partition exists. (32,32,64) aligned measures 1.0063/1.0043/1.0229 and (32,48,48) misaligned measures 1.2493/1.2521/1.2346. Same k, same op set, neither even; only alignment separates them.

VERDICT 4 -- the slab model holds on rvv and fails on gemmini, as predicted. rvv |err| mean 0.029 median 0.008 over 35 cells (the max 0.315 is conv_modules.0, IC=3, where OC is not the only cost driver). gemmini |err| mean 0.543 median 0.551 max 1.325 over 40 cells -- the model is not merely imprecise there, it is the wrong functional form.

MECHANISM, measured without any baseline: inside a single binary, tile time divided by that tile ceil(w/32) slab count is constant to CV 0.3-3.2% per operator across widths 8..112 on rvv (median deviation from the ceil(w/32) staircase 0.5%); the same quantity on gemmini has CV 19-49% (median deviation 26.3%). A 16-wide rvv tile costs exactly what a 32-wide one costs.
STRUCTURAL LOSS at OC=32: ceil(32/32)=1, so no 2-way split can be rvv-aligned. Measured 1.685/1.974/1.970/1.826 against a predicted 2.0. Documented as a structural loss, not a candidate partition.

BSS CONFOUND BOUNDED: the same (op,partition) cell measured in 3 different binaries reproduces to <=0.40% on rvv (3 cells x 3 binaries), so the necessarily cross-binary aligned-vs-misaligned comparison is safe there. On gemmini 7 of 9 repeated cells agree to <=0.54% but all three conv_modules.4/.5/.6 cells in binary M1P sit 9.7-11.7% high -- one binary, one backend, consistent with the known BSS-layout shift.

NOT MEASURED: concurrency (every tile ran serially on one hart, so no placement or bandwidth effect is in these numbers); any backend other than rvv and gemmini_q31; any model other than dronet; OC axes other than 32/64/128; any split axis other than OC.

TOOLING BUG (rvv): tile_sizes=[32,96] on conv_modules.8 returns a wrong result (max_abs_err=6 vs 0), reproduced in isolation as fq 440 with that operator the only split in the binary. conv_modules.7 [32,96] is implicated by elimination. The mirror [96,32] is correct everywhere, as is [32,96] on the 1x1 conv_modules.9. Three runs were excluded by the accuracy gate; no excluded run contributed a cell.

platform: AWS F2 f2.6xlarge x4, f2_quad_hetero_norose_tacit_q31_60mhz (agfi-0662319f4b07483a7), 4 harts: 0/1 rocket+gemmini_q31 (no vector), 2/3 rocket+saturn V256D128 (no gemmini)
job: fq 450-457 (8 jobs). fq 442-449 were an earlier, misconfigured submission of the same 8 binaries -- see infra_bug
question: Does splitting a conv along OH (output ROWS) beat splitting it along OC (output channels), for convs whose OC is at or below the backend's blocking quantum?
placement: every tile serial on one hart (work conservation, no concurrency tax)
metric: work_ratio = sum(tile times)/unsplit time, divided by the binary's drift factor = geometric mean over the convs THAT binary left unsplit, against B0. Drift ranged 1.000-1.022 except ohA/P at 1.116 (uniform 1.095-1.138 across all six monitors -- the BSS-layout shift, removed)
implementation: apply_split_hint._split_conv2d_s8_oh + generate_skeleton's mb_ohtile_conv2d_s8 helper. Activations are NCHW, so a row band is contiguous at NEITHER end: the tile gathers a pre-padded input window, runs the ordinary curated kernel with PH=PW=0, and scatters the output band into the parent's OC channel planes. Padding is materialised in BOTH dims -- rows because per-tile padding is asymmetric and one PH cannot say that, columns because gemmini's curated conv falls back to a scalar loop unless PH==PW.
numerical_gate: spike, both arms, all four split trees: rvv max_abs_err=0 (bit-identical to unsplit); gemmini reproduces the unsplit arm's signature exactly (2 / 0.0357142873) at k=2, and 1 / 0.0179 at k=4 -- inside the arm's MB_DRIFT_ATOL=2 budget but NOT bit-exact, because a different window re-tiles gemmini's hardware im2col. Also proved in numpy over 41 partitions x 10 dronet conv shapes, including uneven and 4-way: bit-identical to unsplit in every case.

copy_rate_ns_per_byte.calibration_set: the K=1 convs, where split and unsplit have IDENTICAL padding (PW=0) so the entire overhead is the gather/scatter
copy_rate_ns_per_byte.summary: 7.6-9.7 ns/B, the SAME on both backends within noise

findings: The halo is NOT the cost. An OH split conserves MACs exactly (disjoint output rows), so the only duplicated work is input rows -- measured at 0.3-1.5 kB against 5-136 kB of total copy traffic, i.e. 0.9-25% of the gather and under 3% for the stride-2 convs. What costs is that NCHW makes a row band non-contiguous at both ends, forcing a gather and a scatter.

rvv, KH>1: OH wins on all seven such convs (0.62-1.23) against OC's 1.00-1.97. For the four OC=32 convs OC cannot beat 2.0 by construction (TILE_OC=vsetvlmax_e32m4=32, so ceil(32/32)=1 slab unsplit and k slabs split); measured 1.68/1.97/1.97/1.82.

rvv, KH=1 stride 2: OH LOSES (2.23 / 1.63 / 1.50 vs OC 1.82 / 1.02 / 1.01). The row-window gather copies (tile_oh-1)*SH+1 rows where the conv reads only tile_oh of them -- 2x the necessary traffic -- and a 1x1 conv has no compute to amortise it.

Part of the rvv OH win is NOT the axis: the tile runs a PRE-PADDED conv with PH=PW=0, which keeps rvv_conv2d_s8_rvv_vsmul_vnclip on its 'all taps in bounds' vectorised strip path. For the small-spatial convs the UNSPLIT call never takes that path at all (OW=4, MB_CONV_TILE=4, PW=1 -> iw0=-1 for the only strip), which is why conv_modules.7/.8 come out at 0.66/0.62. Materialising padding is worth up to ~1.6x on rvv with no split at all -- a bigger and simpler win than either axis.

gemmini: OC wins on all ten convs. The gemmini convs are 49-260 us, the copies are 7.6-17 ns/B, and there is no border path to win back -- gemmini's cost floor is its own NCHW<->NHWC transpose, which an OC split duplicates but which is already only part of the total.

OH cost is FLAT in split degree where OC is a staircase: conv_modules.0 on rvv goes 1.225 (k=2) -> 1.237 (k=4) while OC goes 1.68 -> 4.0 (slab model). Same on gemmini: 1.334 -> 1.329. So OH buys k-way parallelism at ~constant work for any k the row count allows.
verdict: Not a blanket default. OH should be the axis for rvv convs with KH>1 -- it is the only axis that can be at or below 1.0 when OC <= the 32-lane quantum, and it stays there as k grows. It should never be chosen on gemmini, nor for KH=1 strided convs on either backend. The scheduler can decide this from the IR with two closed forms and one calibrated constant per backend; see cost_model.

cost_model.OC: work_ratio ~= sum_i ceil(w_i/Q) / ceil(OC/Q); Q=32 rvv, Q=16 gemmini
cost_model.OH: work_ratio ~= 1 + (gather_B + scatter_B) * rate / T_unsplit, with gather_B = IC*sum_i window_rows_i*(IW+2*PW), scatter_B = OC*OH*OW, rate ~= 9 ns/B measured. Subtract a border credit on rvv when the unsplit conv's only ow-strip starts at iw0<0.
cost_model.decision: pick argmin over the two, per (op, backend); refuse OH when KH < SH

next_steps: Gather only the rows the conv actually reads when KH < SH (compact and call with SH'=1 for KH=1). Predicted to remove ~half of the 219/70/46 us overheads that make OH lose on the three 1x1 convs -- unvalidated, no FPGA budget left.
Materialise conv padding unconditionally on rvv, independent of splitting.
NHWC activations would make an OH tile a pure pointer offset at both ends and delete this whole cost class.

question: Do the per-operator split work ratios compose into an end-to-end makespan, and how much of the OH win is the pre-padding rather than the row split?
gates: all three: entries==dispatch count, Zephyr PASS, kernel_picks=gemmini_tiled_conv, max_abs_err e2eU/e2eM=2 (hetero, gemmini budget) padE=0 (pure rvv, bit-exact)

e2e.scheduler: greedy earliest-completion list schedule over 4 harts (2 gemmini + 2 saturn), durations = this study's measured per-tile times
e2e.makespan_source: XPURT trace span (max end - min start); 1 tick = 1 us to within 1%, calibrated on the serial runs where span must equal the summed dispatch time (0.9895-0.9929 us/tick)

best_per_axis.assignment: OC 2-way on conv_modules.0/.1/.2/.5/.8; the other five convs unsplit; NO OH anywhere

e2e.composition: the per-op numbers compose to within 4% on the SPEEDUP ratio (1.207 measured vs 1.253 predicted). Both arms sit ~6.9-7.5 us/dispatch ABOVE prediction (+145 us on 21 dispatches, +195 us on 26); the serial runs showed only 2.7-3.1 us/dispatch, so roughly 4 us/dispatch is the cost of cross-hart dispatch that a serial work-conservation measurement cannot see. It is a per-dispatch additive term, not a scaling error, which is why the ratio survives better than the absolute makespan.

why_no_OH_end_to_end: On this SoC gemmini is 1.5-14x faster than rvv on every dronet conv, so a makespan-optimal schedule puts every conv on a gemmini hart -- and OH loses on gemmini for all ten convs. The axis search (measured costs, my scheduler) picked OC for 5 convs and unsplit for 5, and OH for none. Forcing OH where it wins on rvv predicts 2439 us against the OC assignment's 1969 us. So OH's per-op win on rvv is real but unreachable by this model on this hetero SoC: the harts where it pays are the ones the scheduler avoids for convs.

padding_attribution.control: dronet_padE -- every conv rewritten as a SINGLE OH tile (k=1): same gather, same PH=PW=0 kernel call, same scatter, no split and no halo. Serial on one rvv hart.
padding_attribution.result: Almost the entire rvv OH win is the PRE-PADDING, not the row split. The split's marginal contribution is +0.002 to +0.050 on every KH=3 conv; pre-padding alone already delivers 0.61-0.89 on conv_modules.4/.5/.7/.8. Only conv_modules.3 (K1 S2) has a large split term (+0.431).
padding_attribution.consequence: Two separate claims, and they must not be merged: (1) the OH AXIS is nearly work-conserving on KH>1 convs -- +0.2% to +5% -- which is much better than OC's staircase and is the honest axis result; (2) the sub-1.0 work ratios are a PADDING optimisation available with no split at all. Anyone building on this should take the pre-padding as its own transform and treat OH purely as a cheap parallelism axis.
padding_attribution.e2e_is_uncontaminated: the e2e best-axis assignment uses no OH tiles, so neither e2e number contains the padding effect

platform: analysis over the dronet graph + the fq 422-471 transpose fit (no new FPGA job)
question: Can the NCHW->NHWC transpose be removed WITHOUT a full layout refactor, by letting a gemmini conv hand NHWC straight to the next gemmini conv?
verdict: NOT WORTH IT. dronet has only THREE direct conv->conv edges (conv1->2, conv4->5, conv7->8) and they carry the SMALL tensors (6272/3136/2048 B). Ceiling is 205 us = 6% of all-gemmini conv time, 10% of transpose time. The expensive transposes are on convs whose neighbours are maxpool/batchnorm/add -- conv0 alone is 37 KB of input.
cost_side: It also requires codegen to know the SCHEDULE's placement: model.c is generated per BACKEND while placement is per DISPATCH, so a conv whose consumer lands on rvv must still emit NCHW. That coupling produces SILENT wrong answers if codegen and schedule drift -- a poor trade for 6%.
conclusion: Eliminating the remaining transpose needs the FULL NHWC change: a layout attribute in the IR plus NHWC variants of maxpool2d_s8 / batchnorm2d_s8 / add_s8 (the elementwise ones are layout-free; batchnorm is per-channel and is actually MORE vector-friendly with C innermost) and a golden verifier that understands both layouts. Scoped, not started.

optimisation_attempts.packed 32-bit stores, input side: 1.04-1.15x unsplit / 1.19-1.24x on the OH windowed path, but conv0 (IC=3, byte fallback, source UNCHANGED) regressed 0.89x on code layout -- net 0.97x

verdict: The transposes are LOAD-bound (strided byte gathers), not store-bound: neither wider stores nor better blocking moves them. ~9.7 cycles/byte is the scalar floor on the in-order Rocket harts, which carry gemmini and NO vector unit. The transpose cannot be meaningfully optimised in place.
action_taken: Reverted both packed paths. Kept the zero-copy OH window (a real measured win: gemmini OH 0/10 -> 6/10 cells beating OC) and the phase instrumentation, which is off by default.
implication: This is the argument for not doing the transpose at all. Chaining NHWC through the conv section leaves only two conversions (the NCHW model input, and the return to NCHW before flatten/linear) = 72% of conv cycles eliminated, 3.53x. A prior note that put this at '205 us / 6%' was wrong twice: it counted only the 3 direct conv->conv edges, ignoring that the chain runs THROUGH maxpool/bn/add/relu, and priced them at the input-transpose rate.

(Q2) Does vsseg beat vlse8/vsse8, or does Saturn crack a strided access per element so the ISA advantage is illusory? (Q3) What is cycles/byte as a function of tensor size and C?
gates: max_abs_err=0 on ALL 1020 timing rows across 5 arms + all 510 round-trip identities h2n(n2h(x))==x bit-exact + MB_DRIFT_ATOL never set (it would hide a real bug: a permutation has no arithmetic to drift) + host-ctypes verify of the gemmini kernel PASS at 8 shapes x 3 trials + spike run 204/204 rows max_abs_err=0 + per-TU ISA isolation (0 vector instructions in the kern_scalar/kern_gemmini objects, 196 in kern_rvv) + check_rvv_avl and check_rvv_vtype clean + 58 modelblaster unit tests pass + arm A vs B identical to 0.00% on every row + arm A vs C (harts 1/3) within 0.13% + each thread printed the hart it actually landed on + the headline speedups recomputed independently in all four arms (2.01x / 8.02-8.06x)
verdict: Q1 YES, and by more than the doc hoped -- but ONLY with segment ops. Bytes-weighted over 17 shapes: scalar floor (lifted blocked TB=32) 7.03 c/B, rvv_strided 3.50 c/B = 2.01x, rvv_seg 0.88 c/B = 8.02x. Q2 YES, decisively: seg beats strided 3.99x pooled, and the gain is a step function of C -- 8.5-23x where C<=8 (one unit-stride vsseg<C>e8 covers the tensor) and 3.5-3.7x where C>=16 (strided vssseg8e8 passes). So the doubt in section 5.2a is HALF right: for vlse8/vsse8 the ISA advantage largely IS illusory (only 2x over a scalar loop), and it is the segment family -- previously unused anywhere in this tree -- that carries the win. corrections_to_the_design_doc.fixed_term: Section 1.1 proposes '~10 cycles/byte, plus a fixed term of roughly 20 kcycles'. Measured directly, the fixed term is under 600 cycles for every variant -- two orders of magnitude smaller. A cost model carrying 20 kcycles of per-dispatch overhead would refuse to split a relayout that splits perfectly well.
corrections_to_the_design_doc.tail_layer_blowup: Section 1.1 reports the output transposes 'degrade to 30-43 cycles/byte on the 512 B - 1.5 KB tail layers (fixed loop/cold-miss overhead over a 512 KB workspace)'. A STANDALONE relayout does not reproduce that at all: 2048 B runs at 7.83/5.83 c/B warm and 7.94/7.90 c/B with 512 KB flushed before every call, and 105 B at 8.66/6.69 warm, 10.10/9.73 flushed. So the tail-layer blowup is NOT intrinsic to the transpose loop; it belongs to something else in gemmini_conv2d_s8 (workspace setup, fence/flush, tiled_conv_auto entry). Worth finding before it is baked into a cost model.
corrections_to_the_design_doc.one_constant_is_wrong: There is no single relayout c/B. It is a function of (hart type, kernel, C): 6.0-8.2 on a gemmini hart, 2.8-4.8 with strided RVV, and 0.18-1.25 with segment RVV where the spread is almost entirely C<=8 (unit-stride vsseg) versus C>=16 (strided vssseg). Stage 2's cost model needs a per-(backend, C-class) cell, not a scalar.
corrections_to_the_design_doc.direction_asymmetry_not_settled: Section 1 has the output transpose (NHWC->NCHW) costing 1.55x the input one, and 1.1 derives 9.8-10.6 c/B for output vs 6.0-6.7 for the packed input path. This experiment CANNOT confirm or refute that for the scalar kernel: its per-direction split moved from 8.04/6.02 to 7.04/7.06 on a 256-byte buffer shift (see reproducibility_caveat). What it does establish is that the scalar transpose costs 7.03-7.05 c/B pooled regardless, and that for the RVV kernels NCHW->NHWC is reproducibly the DEARER direction (strided 4.14 vs 2.86; segment 0.85 vs 0.90) -- the strided-store side is worse than the strided-load side, which is the opposite of what the in-conv brackets implied.
corrections_to_the_design_doc.cited_code_does_not_exist: Section 9 says the gemmini lift should take 'the mb_gem_put4 packed-store path' and section 1.1 cites gemmini_conv2d_s8_gemmini_tiled_conv.c:143-152 as 'why the packed store path needs IC%4==0'. Neither is in HEAD: `git log -S mb_gem_put4` on that file returns nothing, :143-152 is the OH-window comment, and kernel_opt_log's gemmini_oh_window_hot_loop_regression entry records that the packed-store experiments were REVERTED. So section 1.1's '6.0-6.7 c/B for the IC%4==0 packed input path' describes a kernel version that no longer exists. Only the TB=32 blocked nest is there to lift, and that is what was lifted.

why_C_equals_3_matters: conv0's input is C=3, the largest activation in dronet and 51.7% of the doc's post-chaining budget. Because NF is legal for every value in 2..8 and not only powers of two, C=3 is a single vsseg3e8 on the FAST path rather than a 2+1 fallback: 0.36 c/B, 11.8x over strided and 22.9x over the scalar floor. Had the decomposition been 'NF=8 or bust', the single most important case in the model would have been the worst-served one.
how_it_was_verified: No graph emits these ops, so the ordinary curated gate cannot see them: rvv and gemmini both use VERIFY_SPIKE_HARNESS, which builds a whole MODEL and compares its final output. modelblaster/microbench/relayout is a standalone Zephyr app that verifies each kernel against the op's own reference_impl at every shape AND asserts the round-trip identity, which needs no reference model at all. It ran first on spike (204/204 rows max_abs_err=0) and then on F2.
infra_bug_found_and_fixed: The first four jobs printed their full table and PASSED within nine minutes and then sat RUNNING on all four lanes until cancelled. Zephyr's main() returning parks the thread and the idle loop spins, so FireSim's completion=exit never fires. The tree's convention is sys_reboot(SYS_REBOOT_COLD) (test_app/src/main.c:189, generate_xpurt_main.py:1405) and the bench was missing it. Fixed and revalidated as job 484. Cost: four lanes held ~11 minutes each before the data was pulled off the run hosts directly and the jobs cancelled.
not_done_deliberately: No graph emits these ops and no model.c changes -- that is the stage-1 contract (C5, byte-identical output). target_affinity is ('gemmini',) and ('rvv',) exactly, matching where the files live; gemmini_q31 has no curated_aliases, so the quad-hetero build would NOT pick up the gemmini kernel today. That is a stage-3 plumbing gap, harmless now, and it must be closed before any NHWC island lands or the island will silently run the scalar reference.
reproducibility_caveat: The SCALAR kernel's per-direction split is a property of the BINARY, not of the transpose. Arms A/B/C give gem_tb32 n2h 8.04 / h2n 6.02 c/B; arm E -- same source plus one sys_reboot() call, which shifted the static buffers +256 B in BSS -- gives 7.04 / 7.06. The shift is -12.4% and +17.2% UNIFORMLY across every shape and every C, i.e. a constant factor on the inner loop, not a cache-set conflict (which would be shape-dependent). Its POOLED cost is unchanged (7.03 -> 7.05), and so is every headline ratio. The RVV kernels do not move at all: their per-direction values are identical to two decimals in all four arms. So: quote the scalar floor pooled, 7.03-7.05 c/B; quote the RVV direction asymmetry, which is reproducible; do NOT quote a scalar direction asymmetry. This was only visible because the exit-fix rebuild accidentally became a third distinct binary -- arms A and B ran byte-identical ELFs and agreed to 0.00%, which measures the FPGA's determinism, not the measurement's robustness.

platform: spike, targets gemmini_q31 and rvv, kernels.c -Os. Instruction-proportional counts.
question: mlp_control's elu has two rvv curated kernels and no gemmini one. How big is the resulting backend asymmetry, and how much of it can a Gemmini-side kernel close?
gates: picks show elu -> curated/scalar_cephes_exp on gemmini_q31 and elu+linear -> curated/direct on rvv; whole-model max_abs_err 6.68e-06 (gemmini_q31, atol_override=1.0) and 2.38e-07 (rvv), both PASS
headline: elu on gemmini_q31 was 21.4x slower than on rvv (23,334 vs 1,093 cycles). Porting the SAME Cephes minimax expf the rvv kernel uses to the scalar unit gets 2.02x; the residual 10.6x is the vector unit itself and is not a coverage gap.
accuracy_justification: This is the only kernel in this campaign that is NOT bit_exact, and the reason is structural. silu_s8/sigmoid_s8/gelu_s8 get bit-exact LUTs because their input domain is 256 values; elu is fp32 with a continuous domain, nothing memoizes, and the whole cost is picolibc's expf. Every replacement for expf returns a different float. So it evaluates the SAME polynomial, with the same constants and the same operation order, that kernels/rvv/rvv_elu_direct.c already declares numeric_drift for -- it does not widen the envelope the rvv arm of a sweep already sits in, it makes the two arms agree. FMA contraction is suppressed with an empty asm barrier on each multiply, because the RVV kernel writes the Horner chain as separate vfmul/vfadd and a contracted scalar version would drift AWAY from it.
uncovered_and_why: mlp_control's `linear` (fp32) is 94% of the model and has NO gemmini_q31 curated kernel: 370,025 cycles vs rvv's 31,519 (11.7x). Left uncovered deliberately. The reference is already a single-accumulator dependent-FMA chain at 8.2 cycles/MAC, which is near the scalar latency bound; going faster needs multiple accumulators, i.e. a different fp32 summation ORDER and therefore a NUMERIC_DRIFT reduction on a control policy's output. That is a judgement for the owner of the sweep, not a coverage hole to quietly fill.

result.why: ViNT's depthwise layers are 5x5 kernels with PH=PW=2 over 2x2 and 4x5 spatial inputs, so 21 of every 25 taps are OUT OF BOUNDS. Precomputing 25 taps per channel (6912 channels) costs more than the four real MACs per output it accelerates, and the `use_tap ?` ternary left in the inner loop blocked the compiler besides.
result.fix: stop touching the out-of-bounds taps at all -- clamp kh/kw to their valid ranges, which depend only on oh and ow. 398887223, 1.15x.

result.attempt: the SAME tap-range clamp that fixed the int8 depthwise
result.why: TWO reasons, and the second is the general one. (a) ViNT's fp16 convolutions are almost all PH=PW=0, so there were no out-of-bounds taps to skip and the tests were predictable and nearly free. (b) kernels.c is compiled -Os, not -O2 (Zephyr default, confirmed in the build's compile_commands.json), and at -Os GCC does not keep the extra loop-invariant range variables in registers -- the disassembly of the clamped version is a wall of sd/ld stack spills. A hoist that pays for itself in tests removed can lose it again in spills.
result.fix: reverted both to the bounds-test form. The optimization is not wrong, it is shape-dependent.

result.why: ViNT's mul_c1_s8 planes are HW = 4, 20, 80, 336 and 1344. At HW=336 an eager table pays 256 evaluations to save 336, which is a wash once the lookup loop is added; only the single HW=1344 dispatch was ever ahead.
result.fix: memoize -- fill an entry the first time its byte value appears, so the cost is distinct*work with distinct <= min(256, HW) and it cannot lose that way. 28911950, 1.02x -- see the honest_verdict below.

result.attempt: SWAR 8-bytes-at-a-time via memcpy(&x, input+i, 8) after aligning in a byte loop
result.why: int8_t* carries alignment 1, so GCC cannot prove the copy aligned and expands it into an unaligned-safe byte-assembly sequence instead of one `ld`. The run-time alignment check bought nothing because the compiler never saw it.
result.fix: load through a may_alias uint64_t* under an explicit alignment GATE (buffers that are not mutually 8-aligned take the plain scalar loop). Emits ld/sd. 3610, 7.36x.

result.attempt: memoized per-channel LUT alone, guard at 32 elements
result.why: a plane shorter than the 256-entry table cannot amortize it, and dronet has two such layers (H*W = 196 and 49).
result.fix: also replace the roundf CALL with fcvt.w.s under the rmm rounding mode, which helps every element table or not, and raise the guard to 128. That layer went to 52126, 3.54x.

honest_verdict_no_fix_found.why: the op's per-element cost is one unpipelined fdiv.s, and its int8 operand's value entropy at ViNT's plane sizes is too high for memoization to remove enough of them. The divide cannot be replaced bit-exactly (multiplying by a precomputed 1/scale_out is a different float), and this op's reference does not even use roundf -- it uses (int32_t)(v>=0 ? v+0.5f : v-0.5f), so the fcvt-rmm substitution that gives mul_s8 1.68x would be a real 1-LSB change here. The kernel is KEPT because it closes the coverage hole and never loses, but 1.02x is what it is worth and it should not be quoted as a win.

transferable_lesson: Three of these five are the same lesson from different directions: on this target the cost of an int8/fp16 elementwise kernel is almost never the arithmetic. It is a libgcc CALL (roundf, __extendhfsf2, __truncsfhf2), an unpipelined fdiv, or address math -- and -Os means any fix that adds live loop-invariant values pays for them in stack spills. Check what the reference actually COMPILES to before deciding what to optimize.

alignment_finding: NEGATIVE, and measured rather than assumed. what_did_not_work: batchnorm2d_s8 REGRESSES 0.78x (996,789 -> 1,280,679), and it is a property of the layout, not a bug. The NCHW kernel keeps ONE 256-entry table live per H*W plane and fills it LAZILY, so its build cost is `distinct <= min(256, H*W)`. Under NHWC the channel changes every element, so every channel's table must be live at once ([C][256]) and lazy filling would need a [C][256] `seen` array whose memset can exceed the plane -- so the NHWC kernel fills eagerly (C*256) and falls back to the per-element expression when H*W cannot amortise that. dronet's middle batchnorm (C=32, H*W=196) loses its memoisation entirely: 231,258 -> 370,773. This eats 12.4% of the conv saving and is fixable in the kernel, not in the layout.

question: Was the tile-offset element-vs-byte theory the cause of vint's sharded accuracy loss?
verdict: NO. The theory was wrong and the 'fix' was a regression. REVERTED.
what_I_got_wrong: I sampled ONE buffer declaration -- `int8_t buf_vint_slice_1[97920]` -- and generalised that every intermediate buffer is a byte array, so pointer aliases needed byte offsets. Buffers are actually emitted with their tensor's OWN C type: `_Float16 buf_vint_conv2d_15[48384]`, sized in ELEMENTS. slice_1 is `int8_t` because that tensor is i8, not because buffers are untyped.
consequence: Scaling elem_offset by dtype size sent tile_1 to offset 48384 in a 48384-ELEMENT buffer -- exactly one past the end -- and vint's error went 10.82 -> 13.12 (rvv pair) and 8.85 -> 16.56 (hetero). The measurement said the fix was wrong and I initially read the movement as 'more sites remain' rather than 'this change is harmful'.
what_would_have_caught_it_sooner: Reading the buffer DECLARATION for the specific tensor being offset, not a sampled one; and treating 'error moved in the wrong direction after a fix' as evidence against the fix rather than as evidence of an additional bug.
still_true_and_kept: There ARE two alias sources (a per-op one and one reading the splitter's recorded elem_offset, the second overwriting the first). That is a real fragility worth knowing -- patching one alone changes nothing -- but neither needed dtype scaling. _DTYPE_BYTES is kept with a note recording that it is NOT needed here and why.

question: Why does a single conv2d_f16 OC split break vint's output?
ROOT_CAUSE: conv2d_f16's call emitter never applies the OC tile weight offset. Both tiles are handed the SAME weight pointer, so tile_1 computes output channels [48,96) using the weights for channels [0,48).

evidence_from_emitted_C.reading: tile_1's weight argument is identical to tile_0's. It should be `vint_conv2d_5_weights_gemmini_q31 + 768` (oc0=48 * IC=16 * KH=1 * KW=1). The OUTPUT offset 64512 (= 48*32*42) is CORRECT, which independently confirms the output alias was never the problem and the earlier byte-scaling theory was wrong.

mechanism: _oc_tile_operands applies `w + oc0*IC*KH*KW` and `b + oc0`, and is called from exactly three emitters -- conv2d_s8 (:3152), and the two fused-conv arms (:3396, :3443). conv2d_f16 reaches none of them; the s8 arm is gated on op['quant'], which f16 ops do not carry. The comment at that call site describes this exact failure: 'every tile reads OC=[0..tile_oc) of the weight tensor, producing 1/n_splits correct outputs and wrong ones elsewhere'.
consistency_with_the_bisect: Predicts partial correctness per op, error proportional to how much of each conv's output is wrong, and additive across splits. Measured: one split 2.787 / 1.246, eight splits 8.85, baseline 0.328.
THE_FIX: Make the conv2d_f16 emitter call _oc_tile_operands, as conv2d_s8 does. This is the FOURTH registration site a new splittable kind must be added to -- after _SPLITTABLE/_SPLITTABLE_BY_AXIS/_DEFAULT_AXIS in apply_split_hint, _OC_SLICEABLE_CONV_OPS/_N_SLICEABLE_LINEAR_OPS in generate_skeleton, and the weight-repack layout query. NOT applied here: two changes were already made badly today and a third rushed one is poor judgement. The diagnosis is complete and the change is small.
acceptance_test_for_the_fix: vint hetero, ONE split (58:OC:72,72) must return to max_abs_err ~0.328, not merely improve. And a unit test asserting tile_1's weight pointer carries a non-zero offset belongs in pipeline/tests/ -- the existing tests cover conv2d_s8 only, which is why this reached hardware.

question: The four networks' unshardable operators are dominated by pointwise ops (silu_s8 x57 in yolov8n, sigmoid x130 in vint) and maxpool2d_s8 (28.9% of DroNet's gemmini time). Both are structurally trivial to tile. What did it take to register them, and are the tiles numerically identical to the unsplit op?
verdict: Two new split axes land and are BIT-EXACT on spike. E (flat element range) covers 47 pointwise kinds; C (channel range) covers maxpool2d_s8. dronet 5 ops split: max_abs_err=0. yolov8_nano 66 ops split (57 silu_s8 + 6 add_s8 + 3 maxpool2d_s8), 155 -> 221 dispatches: max_abs_err=0.
gates: dronet rvv, 5 ops split (1 pool C + 4 pointwise E): max_abs_err=0 max_rel_err=0
yolov8_nano rvv, 66 ops split: max_abs_err=0 max_rel_err=0, n=75600
dronet gemmini_q31, same 5 ops: max_abs_err=2 max_rel_err=0.0357142873 -- IDENTICAL to the UNSPLIT control on the same arm, i.e. pre-existing gemmini drift that the split does not move
modelblaster pipeline+tests suite: 218 passed (was 198) with the same 4 pre-existing failures at baseline
why_they_were_not_splittable: Nothing structural. The split machinery grew out of the conv campaign, so the only axes that existed were OC, OH and N -- all of which name a dimension of a conv or linear SHAPE. A pointwise op's IR shape is a single flat 'n' and a pool's channel key is 'C', so neither could resolve a splitter at all. 47 pointwise kinds needed ZERO per-kind emitter work once the axis existed.
the_mechanism: A split tile needs three things: narrowed shape, offset output pointer, offset input pointer(s). The splitter does the first; the existing tile offset-alias does the second; the third is the only new codegen, and it is done ONCE for all 47 kinds by redirecting the op's operand names through generate_skeleton's _shim_override (consulted first by ptr_for), rather than editing 47 emitters. maxpool2d_s8 needs its own input offset because a pool's input planes (IH*IW) and output planes (OH*OW) are different sizes -- 50176 vs 11664 on DroNet's 56x56 -> 27x27.
why_C_is_not_OC: Registering the pool under the existing OC axis would have made profile_loader price it with the output-channel SLAB model, ceil(w/q)/ceil(W/q). DroNet's maxpool has C=32, exactly the rvv quantum, so that model reports both halves of a 2-way split as a full slab each -- i.e. that splitting the single most expensive gemmini op in the network is worth 1.00x. A pool's cost is linear in C; the separate axis is how the cost model is told so.
safety: _assert_flat_pointwise re-derives the pointwise property from operand extents at split time, so a reduction wearing a flat (in,out,n) signature -- mse_loss, frobenius_norm, hinge_loss, huber_loss -- is refused even if someone adds it to the registry
The OC-under-NHWC layout guard was extended to C by name: a channel range is contiguous in nchw and strided in nhwc for a pool exactly as for a conv

E is the only axis with no layout precondition at all -- a flat element range is contiguous under every permutation of the axes, which is the same fact act_layout.LAYOUT_AGNOSTIC_OPS records from the other direction

apply_split_hint._POINTWISE_KINDS and generate_skeleton._E_SLICEABLE_ELTWISE_OPS are independent literals with a test asserting they agree; a kind in the first and not the second raises at codegen instead of emitting tiles that all write at offset 0
tests_added: 20 (10 IR-level in test_apply_split_hint.py, 10 emitted-C in test_split_codegen_offsets.py), including the pool's different-input-and-output-offset trap and a fixture assertion that the pool subsamples, since a stride-1 fixture cannot distinguish the two offsets at all

question: Registering the pool `C` split axis let two tiles of one maxpool run on two gemmini harts at once for the first time. Is that safe?
verdict: NO, and the split found it. DroNet on a gemmini PAIR measured max_abs_err=72 against that arm's own unsplit baseline of 2, while every arm with at most ONE gemmini hart (rvv+rvv, rvv+gemmini) was unchanged. Root cause: kernels/gemmini_q31/gemmini_q31_maxpool2d_s8_gemmini_tiled_conv_pool.c holds `static elem_t ws_input[512KB]` and `ws_output[512KB]` SHARED, while the conv kernel beside it has held one slot per hart since the conv split landed. Two tiles overwrite each other's image mid-transpose.
the_discriminator: The error moved ONLY on the two-gemmini-hart arm. dronet rvvpair err=0, dronet hetero err=2 (unchanged), dronet gempair err=2 -> 72. One gemmini hart cannot race itself; that is what makes this a concurrency bug and not an arithmetic one, and it is why spike -- which runs the split serially on one hart -- reported the baseline's max_abs_err=2 exactly and saw nothing.
fix: One workspace slot per hart, indexed by arch_proc_id(), copying the pattern already in gemmini_conv2d_s8_gemmini_tiled_conv.c (MB_GEM_WS_SLOT). ws_weights stays shared deliberately: every hart writes the identical constant +2, so the init is idempotent. Single-hart builds keep exactly one slot. Verified behaviourally neutral: the curated verify gate passes identically with and without the fix (max_abs_err=2 both, maxpool cycles 1305652 vs 1304755 = 0.07%).
pre_existing_and_NOT_fixed: 25 other gemmini kernels hold the same shape of shared static workspace with no per-hart slot -- every im2col_full_C and bn_epilogue variant, the three cat*_c1 mvin_scale kernels, both tiled_matmul linears, and the nhwc pool and conv. They are latent for the reason this one was: their ops are either unsplittable or never scheduled concurrently. rvv is mostly clean, with one exception worth naming: rvv_silu_s8_direct memoises a 256-entry LUT in shared statics keyed on the quant params, so two DIFFERENT silu ops on two harts can each read a table built for the other's scales. That hazard predates this work (57 silu dispatches were always concurrently schedulable) and is NOT introduced by the E axis, whose same-op tiles carry identical params and are therefore benign.
two_traps_hit_while_fixing_it: REGENERATING kernels.c to pick up the kernel edit silently DEMOTED add_s8 from the curated gemmini_resadd to reference_impl, because that kernel now fails the spike verify harness (max_abs_err=67) on a PRISTINE tree -- bisected by reverting each edit in turn, and reproduced with zero local modifications. The on-disk kernel_picks.json predates that. Every already-measured arm used gemmini_resadd, so regenerating would have changed the baseline out from under the comparison. Written up as experiments/shard_dim/scripts/splice_kernel.py: replace one block in kernels.c, never regenerate.

The first splice inserted the curated source VERBATIM and the link failed with `undefined reference to kernel_maxpool2d_s8_dronet_gemmini_q31` -- generate_kernels mangles every kernel symbol by model name and Zephyr staging mangles again by backend. It failed loudly, which is the only reason this is a footnote rather than a measurement taken against a kernel nobody called. splice_kernel.py now recovers the suffix from the block it is replacing.

what_is_left: Changing gemmini kernel CODE moves the answer while changing gemmini kernel DATA does not. Data padding does not shift code; editing those kernels relocates every function linked after them. So the remaining candidates are code-placement effects on the rvv path -- alignment of a hot loop, or an instruction-timing-dependent defect in the Saturn vector unit that spike cannot model. Note dronet's activation buffers carry NO alignment attribute (25 plain declarations in buffers.c) and its conv and maxpool both use strided vector access (vlse8/vsse8).

method_note: Four hypotheses were formed from correlation and each was killed by a discriminating test. question: Every sharded schedule in this campaign has been placed using tile costs DERIVED from the unsplit parent by a model. Running a split tree on ONE hart measures each tile in isolation. How wrong was the model?

the_control_is_the_point: Unsplit ops are carried through the projection 1:1, so their error must be ~0. On vint it is -0.0% and on dronet -2.5%, which licenses reading their axis rows. platform: AWS F2 f2.6xlarge, f2_quad_hetero_norose_tacit_q31_60mhz; dronet int8, measured-tile-cost schedules
job: phase 4 (24 cells, all on measured tile costs)
question: Reading the Gantt charts, dronet's conv_modules.0 tiles look SLOWER on the gemmini pair than the single gemmini tile in the hetero pair -- even though gemmini is the better target for that op. Why?
verdict: Because the two pairs split that conv on DIFFERENT AXES, and OH beats OC for it on gemmini by ~12%. gempair splits conv_modules.0 as OC 16,16 and each gemmini tile measures 0.886 / 0.881 ms; hetero splits it as OH 28,28 and its gemmini tile measures 0.781 ms. Same op, same hardware, 0.781 vs 0.886.
why: An OC tile computes a subset of output channels and must therefore read the ENTIRE input; an OH tile reads only its own row band plus the halo. On gemmini, where 87% of conv time is NCHW<->NHWC layout conversion, re-reading the whole input for half the channels is the more expensive half of that trade.
the_consequence_that_matters: The per-pair conv split args used throughout this campaign were inherited VERBATIM from the pre-fix campaign, whose best-axis search ran against the cost model that measured tile costs have now shown under-prices OC and OH by 37-45% on gemmini. So gempair's choice of OC for conv_modules.0 is very likely stale rather than optimal, and the 24 single-hart split-tree profiles from phase 3.5 are exactly the input needed to redo that search on measurements instead of a model.
found_by: A reader noticing that one colour's blocks were longer in one panel than another, which is the comparison the chart is FOR. It only became askable once tiles of one op shared a colour.
two_tooling_defects_found_in_the_same_pa: pair_gantt.py built its colour map PER ROW from sorted(parents) of that row's own split set. The sets differ per machine pair (dronet splits 14 ops on the rvv pair, 12 on the gemmini pair, 7 on hetero), so the same hue meant a DIFFERENT op in each row -- the chart invited exactly the cross-config comparison it could not support. It also wrapped a 10-colour cycle over 14 parents, so purple was both conv_modules.0 and maxpool1 in ONE panel. Fixed: one map for the whole figure, hatching to extend the palette.

An earlier version named the tile colour `col`, shadowing the enclosing loop's COLUMN index, so every left-hand panel was titled SHARDED. Numbers correct, label wrong -- the class of defect that survives review. Caught by looking at the rendered image.
two_observations_not_yet_explained: yolov8_nano runs 8 of 230 dispatches on a hart DIFFERENT from the one the schedule assigned (222/230 match); dronet matches 35/35 and 33/33. Unknown whether this is the runtime's unbound-work path rebalancing or placement drift.

The per-dispatch predicted_start_ms / predicted_duration_ms fields printed in the uartlog trace sum to ~0.004 ms against a 4.242 ms actual makespan -- roughly 1000x too small, consistent with a ms/us unit confusion in what is baked into the C dispatch table. job: 8 single-hart profiles: {dronet,yolov8_nano} x {all-OC,all-OH} x {rvv hart, gemmini hart}
question: The per-pair conv split axes were chosen against a cost model that measured tiles have since shown under-prices OC and OH by 37-45% on gemmini. Redone on measurement, does the axis choice change?
verdict: The per-BACKEND divergence is real and now measured, but the inherited choices were mostly RIGHT. dronet on rvv splits 5 OC / 5 OH; on gemmini it is 9 OC / 1 OH. gempair's inherited all-OC is VINDICATED, and rvvpair's inherited axes agree with the measured optimum on 8 of 10 convs. One genuine improvement found: conv_modules.8 inherited OC but measures 1.60x faster on OH (rvv 1.293 -> 0.808 ms).
method: Two trees per network -- every splittable conv on OC, then every one on OH -- each run on ONE hart per backend. A single-hart run times each tile in isolation, so summing a conv's tiles gives its real cost under that axis on that backend. No model anywhere in the loop. Replaces a search whose comparison was modelled.
two_claims_of_mine_that_this_CORRECTS: I reported conv_modules.0 as 'OH beats OC on gemmini by 12%' from comparing a gempair OC tile (0.886 ms) against a hetero OH tile (0.781 ms). Those are not comparable -- in hetero the OH split puts one tile on rvv and one on gemmini, so the gemmini tile carries a different share. Summing both tiles on the SAME hart gives OC 1.668 vs OH 1.676: a TIE.
I called gempair's all-OC choice 'very likely stale'. It is not: gemmini prefers OC on 9 of 10 convs by measurement.
two_gaps_in_this_search: EVEN SPLITS ONLY. The generator emitted a 2-way split only when the axis extent was even, so dronet's three convs with OH=7 (conv_modules.4/5/6) were never evaluated on OH -- their 'OC' verdict is ABSENCE OF DATA, not a result. The inherited args split one of them 3,4, which the splitter supports via tile_sizes. Fixing the search means emitting uneven partitions.

yolov8_nano's all-OH profile returns max_abs_err=35 where every other profile reads 0. Splitting all 45 OH-eligible yolo convs is numerically WRONG -- a defect that only appears at that scale. yolo's OH column is unusable until bisected. dronet's OH profiles are clean at 0, so the dronet table stands.

job: 951 split operators, each with all four measurements: unsplit + tiles on ONE hart (serial{E,P}_{base,shardec{R,G,H}}) and unsplit + tiles on the PAIR (<net>_<pair>_{base,shardec})
question: plot_shard_benefit's per-operator panel is measured on single-hart runs, so its 'ideal 2-hart speedup' assumes the tiles never contend and the second dispatch is free. How much of that ideal survives once both harts really run at once, and where does the rest go?
method: Per parent op the identity achieved = ideal x (U_cc/U_iso) x (max t_iso/max t_cc) x (max t_cc/S) holds exactly, so each term is separately measured, not modelled: ideal=U_iso/max(t_iso) from the isolated arms, achieved=U_cc/span from the pair, and the three factors are baseline shift, contention, launch+sync. Aggregated as geometric means so the ladder composes exactly. Tiles are matched by tile INDEX to the isolated arm whose backend matches the hart they landed on, so hetero is not averaged across backends.
verdict: The isolated profile is a GOOD predictor on homogeneous pairs and a bad one on the hetero pair, and the reason is start skew, not contention. rvv+rvv 1.966 -> 1.857 achieved (94% of the promise), gem+gem 1.796 -> 1.709 (95%), rvv+gem 1.528 -> 1.091 (71%). Contention between the two tiles is small and uniform at x0.985-0.990 (1.0-1.5%) on ALL THREE pairs -- an order of magnitude less than the +6% the isolated dronet conv_modules.0 2x3 suggested, so that earlier number was specific to one large gemmini conv and does not generalise. The whole hetero shortfall is the launch+sync term, x0.724: the span of a hetero tile pair is 38% longer than its slowest tile, i.e. the two tiles do not start together because one hart is still busy. On the homogeneous pairs the same term is only x0.956/x0.964. The baseline term is x0.998-1.002 everywhere: an unsharded operator is NOT measurably slower just because the other hart is busy.
consequence: Two actionable things. (1) On homogeneous pairs the cheap single-hart split profile can be trusted to within ~5%, so the axis search does not need 2-hart runs. (2) The hetero pair's sharding problem is a SCHEDULING problem: the tiles are ready but one hart is not, so the fix is start alignment (co-scheduling the tiles of one op), not a better split axis or a memory-system change. This also explains the E2E table, where hetero never exceeds 1.13x on any network.

platform: AWS F2, f2_quad_hetero_norose_tacit_q31_60mhz_pcim (TACIT tracing needs the PCIM bitstream; the non-PCIM quad returns a 100%-zero stream)
question: NOTES_3NET.md recorded that a 3rd rclc executor OR a 3rd timer collapses concurrency to 0.4%, root-caused only as 'rcl_wait blocks on something' and never fixed. What is it, and can it be fixed?
verdict: ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED. It is NOT middleware blocking and NOT lock contention -- it is CPU starvation. Three facts compose: (1) rmw_wait takes its `available_contexts == 0` branch on every call, because need_to_be_ran is only ever set from subscriptions/services/clients and this harness has zero of all three, and that branch calls uxr_run_session_timeout(session, 0) -- NON-BLOCKING -- then returns, so rcl_wait never waits; (2) rclc_executor_spin is `while(true){spin_some();}`, so it becomes a hot loop that never yields; (3) dronet and mlp_control are both pinned to hart 2 at equal priority K_PRIO_PREEMPT(1) with CONFIG_TIMESLICING unset (Zephyr default n), and a preemptive scheduler does not preempt an equal-priority thread. Whichever executor starts first owns hart 2 forever. TACIT proved (2)+(3) directly: hart 2's trace decoded to 130,426,009 instructions whose hottest basic blocks are mb_conv2d_s8_tiled_direct and mb_requant_i32m4 -- DRONET's own conv kernel. The core was never idle and the scheduler was never entered, which is why every 'is the middleware wedged' hypothesis was wrong.
fix: Guest-side only, no third-party patch: CONFIG_TIMESLICING=y + TIMESLICE_SIZE=1 + TIMESLICE_PRIORITY=0, plus CONFIG_RISCV_V_DECOUPLED_LAZY=y, plus CONFIG_MICROROS_NODES/PUBLISHERS=4 so the third node can exist at all. Measured: mlp_control 0 -> 14 iterations, yolov8_nano completes (319,774 cycles).

refuted.H1_H5_unsynchronised_sessions: REFUTED by the trace. UXR_LOCK/UXR_UNLOCK really are empty macros in this build and rmw_wait really does walk every session from every thread, but hart 2 was executing dronet's conv kernel, not middleware, so that race is not what starved mlp_control.
refuted.H2_static_input_buffer_pool: REFUTED by source, no build spent. The pool is allocated from only in callbacks.c on_topic/on_request/on_reply; this harness has 0 subscriptions/clients/services and NO_PUBLISH=1.
refuted.H4_threads_not_pinned: REFUTED. main.c:1223-1256 uses K_FOREVER -> pin -> start, the correct order.
refuted.rmw_wait_blocking_patch: TRIED AND REVERTED. Making the metatraffic branch honour the caller's timeout HANGS: it propagates UXR_TIMEOUT_INF into uxr_run_session_timeout, which blocks forever. The upstream 0 is there for that reason. Job 812 wedged at 24 min against a ~7 min healthy run. The guest-side fix alone is sufficient, so the third-party file is left untouched.

question: The 3-net starvation fix (TIMESLICING) exposed a fault in dronet's RVV conv. Is it lost VECTOR state across the V context switch, or something else?
verdict: NOT vector state -- it is exactly one SCALAR GPR clobbered by a trap taken mid-vector-kernel. Proved by arithmetic on three independent faults, all in mb_conv2d_s8_tiled_direct, all on a vector MEMORY op whose base/stride register holds a value the kernel's own arithmetic cannot produce. cfg3xF vsse8.v v2,(a7),a0 mtval=0x3d02e67d70 needs (n*OC+oc_base)=82,874,420 where the enclosing `while (oc_base < oc_end)` bounds it to <= OC <= 256. cfg3xG vle8.v v1,(t3) mtval=0x480000000 = DRAM_BASE + exactly 2^34, only bits 31 and 34 set, not the shape of any weight offset. cfg3xH (this job, cfg3xG config with CONFIG_STARTUP_TACIT=n) mtval=0x7bfdfbfbf8, not in DRAM at all, bytes f8 fb fb fd 7b reading as int8 tensor data in a scalar register. A stale vstart cannot explain any of them: vstart is bounded by VLMAX (256 for e8m8 at VLEN=256), so it can move an address by at most 256 bytes, not 2^34.
fix: none in this entry -- diagnosis only
refuted: (1) vreg[32][CONFIG_RISCV_VECTOR_MAX_LEN/8] overflow: the quad-hetero bitstream is WithRocketVectorUnit(256,128) per soc/src/main/scala/RoSEConfigs.scala:450, VLEN=256 matches CONFIG_RISCV_VECTOR_MAX_LEN=256, vse8.v e8m8 writes exactly 4x256=1024 B into a 1024 B array. No overflow. (2) shared arena/pool between dronet and mlp_control: each model has its own buffers.c with uniquely-named statics, and the RVV kernels hold no static scratch. (3) thread/stack aliasing: thread_a/b/c and stack_a/b/c are distinct, 1 MB each, and the branches that reuse them are mutually exclusive #if arms. (4) stale-vstart, by the bound above.
still_open: Whether the residual bare-tick hazard (convfix-007) can still fire under a sched-lock-only guard.

question: Does the dispatch guard that every OTHER harness in the tree already ships remove this crash class from harness_microros?
verdict: YES for the crash, NO for a clean run. Same source, same pinning (dronet+mlp_control both on hart 2), only difference is k_sched_lock()/k_sched_unlock() around each DISPATCH_FNS call: cfg3xH faults with mcause=7 within ~16 s of boot; cfg3xJ runs the full 600 s timeout with NO mcause at all. But cfg3xJ then fails to complete -- only 2 of 3 broker sessions come up (s=1, s=0; s=2 never) and it stalls. cfg3xJ ALSO replaced net A's whole-loop irq_lock() with the per-dispatch guard, which is the one collateral change and the likely cause of the stall; net A (yolov8 on hart 0) is alone on its hart and never needed the guard.
fix: modelblaster/harness_microros/src/main.c: MICROROS_DISPATCH_GUARD (default 1) -> k_sched_lock()/k_sched_unlock() around each single dispatch call. NOT irq_lock(): include/zephyr/irq.h:259 redefines it to z_smp_global_lock() under CONFIG_SMP, which serialises the harts (measured, FPGA job 375). Escalation knob MICROROS_DISPATCH_GUARD_IRQ adds arch_irq_lock() (a genuine per-hart mstatus.MIE clear, include/zephyr/arch/riscv/arch.h:257) for the residual bare-tick hazard of convfix-007.
refuted: That the fix belongs in Zephyr's arch/riscv V context switch. convfix-006 already wrote, hardware-proved AND REVERTED exactly that patch; convfix-007 then showed the hazard survives it.
still_open: The 3-executor arm has never completed on F2, with or without this fix. cfg3xI (no source change at all, dronet hart 2 / mlp hart 3 / broker hart 1) also stalled after all 3 sessions came up, so the stall is not obviously caused by the guard.

platform: AWS F2 f2_quad_hetero_norose_tacit_q31_60mhz_pcim; harness_microros Config B
job: static feasibility check of all 8 wl_sweep families against the harness, plus one live run (wl_control_mix, fq 849)
question: The wl_sweep matrix is 8 workload families. Which of them can the micro-ROS baseline express and actually run?
verdict: 5 of 8 are expressible; 3 are not, and the first one actually RUN exposed a latent Zephyr defect. Expressible as-is: control_mix, perception_heavy, saturation, vint_intro, vint_multi. Blocked: scale_ladder (6 networks against a hard 2-3 limit at examples/microros_demo/run.sh:84, NET_A/B/C being compile-time), and tight_loop + bimodal (sub-millisecond periods).
danger: The sub-millisecond block is SILENT, not an error. harness_microros/src/main.c:620-621 does `one_shot = (period_ms == 0)` and `period_ns = RCL_MS_TO_NS(period_ms)` on a uint64_t of INTEGER milliseconds, so mlp_control_sa's 0.032-0.048 ms period truncates to 0 and the network is converted from periodic to ONE-SHOT without complaint. A separate hard floor: the executor loop carries k_msleep(1) at main.c:644. Anyone running tight_loop or bimodal under micro-ROS would measure a different workload than the one they named.
live_run: wl_control_mix (yolov8_nano_sc one-shot, dronet_se @39ms, mlp_control_sd @2ms) BUILDS clean -- the first time the harness has linked scaled variants -- all three nodes init, all three sessions come up, and yolov8_nano_sc completes in 59978 us. Then hart 2 dies: mcause=2 illegal instruction, mtval=0xc22022f3, mepc=0x8000dd80.
root_cause: mtval 0xc22022f3 decodes as `csrr t0, vlenb` -- CSR 0xC22, opcode 0x73 (SYSTEM/CSRRS). arch/riscv/core/isr.S:244-248 routes ONLY opcode 0x57 (OP-V, vector arithmetic) to the vector trap handler and falls through to _v_disp_done for anything else, so a first-touch of the vector unit via a vector CSR READ is never granted access and dies as illegal. This is the same defect reported (and deliberately not fixed) during the RVV context-corruption campaign, which enumerated the missed cases as 0x07/0x27 vector load/store; 0x73 vector-CSR reads are a THIRD missed case. It surfaced now because the scaled-variant kernels probe vlenb where the base dronet/mlp_control kernels never did -- the same probe ExecuTorch's XNNPACK RVV micro-kernels make, per samples/executorch/executor_runner/prj.conf.
fix_not_applied: Extend the isr.S router to accept, besides 0x57: opcode 0x07/0x27 with funct3 in {0,5,6,7} (vector load/store), and opcode 0x73 whose CSR field is a vector CSR (0x008-0x00A vstart/vxsat/vxrm, 0xC20-0xC22 vl/vtype/vlenb). NOT applied here: arch/riscv is linked by every model in the tree and an ExecuTorch campaign is building against it right now. Landing it under a running campaign is how you get an unattributable regression.
consequence: The micro-ROS baseline generalises to 5 of the 8 families, but none of them can be trusted until the isr.S router is fixed, because every scaled variant probes vlenb. tight_loop and bimodal need a sub-millisecond timer path and cannot be represented at all today. scale_ladder needs a harness that is not hard-wired to three networks.

question: Does ExecuTorch actually generate RVV code on this target, or is `XnnpackPartitioner()` in every exporter measuring ARM/x86-oriented scalar fallbacks? This decides whether the whole ET-vs-ModelBlaster comparison means anything.
gates: the RVV micro-kernel sources must be compiled WITH the vector extension -- checked on a real compile line, not just the cmake option
kernel selection must not depend on a runtime cpuinfo/hwcap probe that cannot work on bare metal
the linked ELF must actually contain vector instructions
verdict: ExecuTorch reaches RVV through XNNPACK, and ONLY through XNNPACK. (1) XNNPACK/CMakeLists.txt:1000 applies `-march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d` as a per-SOURCE COMPILE_FLAGS property to ALL_RVV_MICROKERNEL_SRCS; per-source flags land LAST on the command line, after Zephyr's own -march, so they win -- verified on the compile line for f32-argmaxpool-9p8x-rvv-u1v.c, which ends `-march=rv64imafdc_zicsr_zifencei ... -march=rv64gcv`. (2) The ucb-bar fork patched src/configs/hardware-config.c:254 to `const bool use_riscv_vector = XNN_ENABLE_RISCV_VECTOR;` with the getauxval hwcap probe commented out, so selection is COMPILE-time and cannot silently fall back to scalar on bare metal. (3) riscv64-zephyr-elf-objdump of the linked zephyr.elf finds 1708 vector instructions. CONVERSELY: the ExecuTorch subbuild's base flags are -march=rv64imafdc (no v) and Zephyr adds -fno-tree-vectorize/-fno-tree-loop-vectorize/-fno-tree-slp-vectorize, so every node the XnnpackPartitioner does NOT take runs as an ExecuTorch PORTABLE kernel that cannot be vectorized at all. The right question per model is therefore how much of the graph XNNPACK takes, not whether RVV exists.
refuted: The premise that `XnnpackPartitioner()` implies no RVV. XNNPACK upstream carries ~300 rvv/riscv micro-kernel sources and the ucb-bar fork enables them; the earlier in-tree note modelblaster/notes/flow_comparison.md had already validated this on the dual-Saturn bitstream.
also_found: XNNPACK_ENABLE_RISCV_GEMMINI, which samples/executorch/executor_runner/CMakeLists.txt sets to ON, does NOT EXIST in any XNNPACK in this tree -- no `gemmini` string in any XNNPACK CMakeLists and no *gemmini* source. It is a no-op. ExecuTorch has no Gemmini path, so harts 0/1 of the hetero bitstream are unusable by it.

platform: AWS F2 f2_quad_hetero_norose_tacit_q31_60mhz (agfi-0662319f4b07483a7; harts 0,1 = Rocket+Q0.31 Gemmini rv64imafdc NO vector, harts 2,3 = Rocket+Saturn VLEN256/DLEN128), lane f2-05
question: The samples/executorch tree was built for a dual-Rocket-SATURN bitstream where every hart had a vector unit. What breaks when it is pointed at the HETEROGENEOUS quad, where the boot hart has no vector unit at all?
gates: uartlog must show MB_ET_HART=2 -- anything else means the ET region is on a Gemmini-only tile
uartlog must show MB_ET_THREADPOOL from=4 to=1 ok=1 -- an unclamped pool hands vector work to unpinned workers on harts 0/1
build must assert XNN_ENABLE_RISCV_VECTOR=1 and XNN_RISCV_VLENB set
verdict: THREE distinct failures, and the first one is NOT fixable by thread pinning. (1) fq 850 died with `mcause: 2, Illegal instruction, mtval 0xc0075d7` immediately after the Zephyr boot banner, before any application print. 0xc0075d7 decodes as OP-V/funct3=7 = `vsetvli a1, zero, e8, m1, ta, ma` -- exactly XNNPACK's VLEN probe in hardware-config.c. It runs that early because ExecuTorch constructs its backend in a C++ STATIC INITIALIZER (backends/xnnpack/runtime/XNNPACKBackend.cpp:207, `auto cls = XnnpackBackend();`) whose ctor calls xnn_initialize(). Static initializers run on the BOOT hart = hart 0 = no vector unit, so no application-level k_thread_cpu_pin can ever help. Fixed by replacing the probe with a build-time -DXNN_RISCV_VLENB=32 (Saturn VLEN 256/8); it is the only vector instruction on the xnn_initialize() path. (2) hardware-config.c would not even ASSEMBLE first: RoSE's zephyr CONFIG_RISCV_V_KERNEL_ONLY strips `v` from the global -march and re-adds it per-file, and hardware-config.c is not a micro-kernel source, so `unrecognized opcode vsetvli, extension v required`. Fixed by adding that one file to XNNPACK's -march=rv64gcv per-source set. (3) The samples' standard single-core trick MP_MAX_NUM_CPUS=1 HANGS here (Zephyr SMP boot spinwaits for every configured hart); replaced with MP_MAX_NUM_CPUS=4 + -DMB_ET_THREADS=1 (ThreadPool::_unsafe_reset_threadpool(1)) + -DMB_ET_PIN_HART=2. k_thread_cpu_pin() on a RUNNING thread is a silent no-op, so the runner creates K_FOREVER, pins, then starts -- the harness_tacit idiom.

job: fq 851 (checksums), fq 853 (MB_ET_SAMPLE_OUTPUT per-element dump), fq 857 (bit-identical repeat of fq 851's ELF)
question: Does the RVV hardware compute what the exported program says? A fast wrong answer is not a result.
gates: the runner must feed the real input (MB_INPUT_BAKED) -- with the stock all-ones fill this comparison is meaningless
a checksum can hide compensating errors, so back it with a per-element dump
distinguish nondeterminism from deterministic divergence by re-running the SAME ELF
verdict: mlp_control, dronet and vint match the x86 host to PRINT PRECISION (|HW-host| 1.5e-07..4.4e-07, i.e. the rounding of printf %f's 6 decimals) -- RVV reproduces the host as exactly as this can resolve. yolov8_nano DOES NOT: ~3e-4 relative on the output sums, and per-element up to 0.37/0.65/0.64 absolute on the three detect heads with 30-46% of sampled elements differing. The mechanism is now pinned: 100% of the differences are EXACT INTEGER MULTIPLES of that head's output quantization step (0.122745 / 0.129619 / 0.127989), ratios 1..5. So this is integer requantization/accumulation-order divergence inside the quantized conv path, NOT fp noise and NOT a layout bug. Consistent with the earlier KernelBench sweep, where ALL checksum mismatches were conv/conv-transposed while activations, matmul and softmax matched exactly.
determinism: fq 857 re-ran the IDENTICAL ELF from fq 851 and reproduced every cycle count and every checksum BIT-FOR-BIT (1512815 / 13941927 / 303143017; checksums 14.791794, -0.030273, 0.478202, -448952.978705, -97813.484649, -19112.570846). So ExecuTorch on this hardware is fully deterministic and the measurement is exactly repeatable.
retracted: An apparent yolov8_nano output change between fq 851 and fq 853 was initially read as nondeterminism. It is not: fq 853 is a DIFFERENT BUILD (MB_XNN_PROFILE=ON, which makes XNNPACK create its runtime with XNN_FLAG_BASIC_PROFILING and take a different execution plan, and MB_EXEC_ITERS=2 vs 3). fq 857 settles it -- same ELF, byte-identical results.
quantization_vs_torch: separately, on the host: mlp_control fp32 max_abs_err 6.68e-06 (identical to ModelBlaster's own MODELBLASTER_VERIFY 6.67572021e-06 -- the two flows agree in fp32); dronet int8 6.60e-03 / cos 0.99991; yolov8_nano int8 3.069 / cos 0.99962; vint int8 0.568 / cos 0.99770. These are XNNPACK pt2e symmetric per-channel PTQ errors and are NOT comparable to MB's verify numbers, which are reported in each model's own output dtype.

platform: AWS F2 f2_quad_hetero_norose_tacit_q31_60mhz, single RVV hart both sides
question: ExecuTorch runs ViNT 25x FASTER than ModelBlaster (673,136,658 vs 17,019,615,052 cycles). Is that an ExecuTorch win, or does it say something about our baseline?
gates: shapes must match: ET vint inputs [1,18,64,85]+[1,3,64,85] = 114240 elements = MB io.npz input (114240,); outputs [1,1]+[1,5,4] = 21 = MB output (21,). They do.
the two conv sets in MB's profile must be checked for duplicated work before blaming the kernels
verdict: It is a statement about the ModelBlaster baseline, not about ExecuTorch. MB's 17.0G cycles are conv2d_s8_pc 7.71G/45.3% (n=65), conv2d_f16 5.11G/30.0% (n=65), linear_s8_pc 1.35G/7.9%, sigmoid_s8 0.99G/5.8%. The two conv sets are DISJOINT by dispatch name (0 overlap), so this is the intended mixed-precision ViNT config -- one EfficientNet encoder int8, the other fp16 -- and NOT duplicated work. The problem is the RATE: MB's largest single dispatch conv2d_86 (N=6, IC=16, 32x42, OC=96, 1x1) is 12.4M MACs in 504,753,595 cycles = ~41 CYCLES PER MAC, roughly two orders of magnitude off what a VLEN=256 int8 machine can do, so conv2d_s8_pc is evidently not resolving to a curated kernel. Even comparing MB's int8 half alone (7.71G) against ET's ENTIRE model gives 11.4x. The ViNT MB baseline is kernel-limited, not architecture-limited, and this ET run is an independent lower bound on the headroom sitting in it.
caveat: The slow-kernel conclusion is INFERRED from cycles/MAC, not read from a kernel-pick dump. Confirming it means re-running MB vint with a kernel-pick gate like the one experiments/shard_dim/scripts/build_one.sh applies to gemmini. Also note ET runs BOTH encoders int8 while MB runs one int8 + one fp16, so ET does strictly less numerical work in one half.

question: The exporter does sys.path.insert(0, MB_REPO) and then imports modelblaster.models.<name>. Is that enough to guarantee the RoSE models are the ones exported?
gates: print and ASSERT the resolved module __file__ lies under MB_REPO before exporting anything
verdict: NO, and it silently failed. The ExecuTorch env carries an editable install (_editable_impl_modelblaster.pth -> an OLDER ModelBlaster tree's src/), and RoSE's modelblaster/ has no top-level __init__.py, so it can only ever be a NAMESPACE package. Python resolves a REGULAR package found anywhere on sys.path in preference to a namespace portion at sys.path[0], so the old tree won: `modelblaster -> <old tree>/modelblaster/src/modelblaster/__init__.py` and `modelblaster.models.dronet -> <old tree>/modelblaster/models/dronet.py`, despite sys.path[0] being RoSE. The trees differ (mlp_control 15, dronet 20, yolov8_nano 162 diff lines; vint identical). The session's first three exports were made against the wrong models and were discarded.
fix: experiments/executorch/scripts/export_mb_models.py binds the package root explicitly (types.ModuleType('modelblaster') with __path__ = MB_REPO/modelblaster, installed into sys.modules) and then asserts os.path.realpath(mod.__file__).startswith(MB_REPO), printing `[provenance] <model> <- <path>`.
