gates: each build dir must own its ExecuTorch/XNNPACK object tree
verdict: NO. ET_BUILD_DIR_PATH defaults to ${ET_DIR_PATH}/cmake-out -- INSIDE the source tree -- so every west build dir shares one ExecuTorch/XNNPACK object tree. A profiling build and a clean build overwrite each other's objects and you link whichever ran last, with no sign in the build log. This was observed directly: after switching variants, hardware-config.c.obj still carried the pre-patch code and the trapping vsetvli encoding 0c0075d7 was still present in a supposedly-fixed ELF.
fix: experiments/executorch/scripts/build_et_elf.sh passes -DET_BUILD_DIR_PATH=$BD/et-cmake-out so each build dir owns its ExecuTorch objects. Also: build gates must read BUILD ARTIFACTS (.config, compile_commands.json, objdump) and not the build log -- an incremental build does not re-run cmake configure, so the message(STATUS)/`Merged configuration` lines are absent from a rerun even though the settings are in force. A gate keyed on those log lines gave a false ABORT on a correct build.

platform: AWS F2 f2_quad_hetero_norose_tacit_q31_60mhz_pcim; harts 0,1 Rocket+Gemmini Q31 (no V), harts 2,3 Rocket+Saturn RVV VLEN256/DLEN128; CONFIG_RISCV_V_DECOUPLED_LAZY=y
job: fq 854 (wlmixV, fixed), fq 858 (wlmixC, router reverted in-place), vs fq 849 (wl_control_mix, pre-fix)
question: wl_control_mix dies at mcause=2 / mtval=0xc22022f3 on hart 2. Is the decoupled-lazy V trap ROUTER in arch/riscv/core/isr.S incomplete, and does completing it fix the workload?
verdict: YES, ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED. mtval=0xc22022f3 decodes as `csrr t0, vlenb` (opcode 0x73 SYSTEM, funct3=010 CSRRS, csr=0xc22) and mepc=0x8000dd80 is the second instruction of kernel_linear_mlp_control_sd_rvv -- the generated RVV prologue probing VLEN to size its stack frame, BEFORE its first vsetvli. mstatus=0x0a00001800 has VS=OFF (and FS=OFF), so this is a legitimate first-touch-of-V trap. isr.S:244-248 tested ONLY `(mtval & 0x7f) == 0x57`, so a 0x73 fell through to z_riscv_fault and killed the thread. Widening the router to OP-V + LOAD-FP/STORE-FP (vector widths) + vector-CSR SYSTEM makes wl_control_mix run to *** PASSED *** with all three networks done: yolov8_nano_sc iters=1 (wall 60129), mlp_control_sd iters=13 (wall 145), dronet_se iters=2 (wall 8824); 280/280 trace slots carry ROS_TRACE_MAGIC, MODELBLASTER_ROS_TRACE_END skipped=0 corrupted, zero mcause lines, 10,180,196,672 cycles. Trace rows: yolov8_nano_sc 147, mlp_control_sd 91, dronet_se 42.
fix: zephyr_ws/zephyr arch/riscv/core/isr.S (commit ceb2b9c3fcc): the CONFIG_RISCV_V_DECOUPLED_LAZY dispatch now routes three encoding classes to z_riscv_v_trap instead of one -- OP-V 0x57; LOAD-FP 0x07 / STORE-FP 0x27 with width funct3 in {0,5,6,7} (vle*/vlse*/vlxei* and the store forms), folded onto one test by masking bit 5; SYSTEM 0x73 with funct3&3 != 0 and csr in {0x008-0x00a, 0x00f, 0xc20-0xc22}. Still clobbers only t0/t1, preserves t2=mstatus. Scalar flh/flw/fld/flq (widths 1-4) and ecall/ebreak/mret/wfi (funct3==0) are explicitly excluded so nothing non-vector can now reach z_riscv_v_trap. Also restores t0=mepc on the fall-through, which the F dispatch below reads under RISCV_NO_MTVAL_ON_FP_TRAP and which this block had already destroyed. Second, related defect fixed in arch/riscv/core/v.c: v_access_allowed()'s owner==_current branch returns true (= grant V) without guaranteeing _current_cpu->arch.v_state is non-zero, and both callers apply v_state AS the grant, so a thread could be told it had access and still resume on a VS==OFF frame -- straight back into the router. It now sets MSTATUS_VS_CLEAN when v_state is zero.
gates: (1) CAUSAL CONTROL, not just before/after: wlmixC is fq 854's OWN ELF with the 118-byte router region overwritten in place by the pre-fix 4-instruction OP-V-only test, NOP-padded -- 91 bytes differ, every symbol, buffer and link address identical (the convfix-003/006 technique). It reproduces the original fault exactly: mcause=2, mtval=0xc22022f3, mepc=0x8000dde8 (= csrr t0,vlenb in kernel_linear_mlp_control_sd_rvv in THIS build), mstatus VS=OFF, hart 2, after yolov8_nano_sc done iters=1 -- the same shape as fq 849. So the router IS the variable; the concurrent harness_microros refactor is not. (2) The reproducer is unchanged by the rebuild: kernel_linear_mlp_control_sd_rvv still opens with `csrr t0, vlenb`, and both ELFs contain exactly 8 vlenb probes. (3) The linked image was disassembled to confirm all six `is_v` branch targets resolve in range. (4) The decision logic was checked against assembler-generated encodings for 39 instructions (13 vector arith/load/store forms, 8 vector CSRs, scalar flh/flw/fld/flq/fsw/fsd, fcsr/frm/fflags, mstatus, ecall/ebreak/mret/wfi, add/lw/sw, fadd.s, fmadd.s) -- every vector form routes, every non-vector form falls through.
refuted: That fixing this belongs anywhere near convfix-006. That patch changed the UNCONDITIONAL IRQ entry/exit path (dropping the eager z_riscv_vstate_save call) that every model in the tree links, which is why it was reverted. This one is entirely inside #if defined(CONFIG_RISCV_V_DECOUPLED_LAZY), and modelblaster/harness_microros/prj.conf:96 is the ONLY config in zephyr-chipyard-sw that sets it -- harness/, harness_xpurt/, harness_tacit/ and samples/executorch/ all compile byte-identical output. Also refuted: that this is the same bug as the convfix/preempt campaign's scalar-GPR corruption. That one is a Saturn hazard that corrupts one register mid-kernel with a garbage address; this one is a software dispatch table that never had a 0x73 arm. They are independent, and the dispatch guard in harness_microros/src/main.c does not mask this (the trap fires on the FIRST V instruction of a kernel, inside the guarded region).
still_open: The router grants V on any hart, including harts 0/1 which have no vector unit -- there a vector CSR read would now trap-loop in z_riscv_v_trap rather than dying with a clear fault. This hazard PRE-EXISTS for OP-V (the 0x57 arm has always done it) and is not reachable in this workload (yolov8_nano_sc's gemmini_q31 path emits no V, and it completes on hart 0 in every run here), but a per-hart has-V guard in z_riscv_v_trap would close it. Also untouched: the residual Saturn preemption hazard of convfix-007.

platform: AWS F2 f2_quad_hetero_norose_tacit_q31_60mhz, ET pinned to hart 2, XNNPACK pthreadpool=1. Per-op from a MB_XNN_PROFILE=ON build (XNN_FLAG_BASIC_PROFILING -> `>>, <op>, <cycles>` per operator per invoke); whole-model totals from the profiling-OFF build.
job: fq 859 (per-op), totals from fq 851; MB side fq 597/601/616
question: ExecuTorch is 1.8-2.6x slower than ModelBlaster on the three convnets. Is that the RVV kernels, or the runtime around them?
gates: op counts must line up between the two flows or it is not like-for-like: dronet 10 conv vs 10 conv; yolov8_nano 63 conv vs 39 Convolution-IGEMM + 24 FullyConnected-GEMM (the 1x1s lower to GEMM) = 63. They do.
totals must NOT be taken from the profiling build -- its execute() bracket is inflated ~500x by HTIF logging (169.6G vs 303M cycles for the same yolov8_nano)
XNN_FLAG_BASIC_PROFILING also changes XNNPACK's execution plan, so the attribution is of a closely-related plan, not the exact one timed
verdict: IT IS NOT THE KERNELS. XNNPACK's RVV convolutions BEAT ModelBlaster's hand-written ones: dronet 4,063,025 vs 7,209,291 (ET 1.77x faster, n=10 both), yolov8_nano 77,864,014 vs 155,470,762 (ET 2.0x faster, n=63 both), mlp_control 4 GEMMs 67,226 vs 4 linears 531,075 (ET 7.9x faster). ExecuTorch gives all of it back three ways. (1) UNFUSED TRANSCENDENTALS: XNNPACK decomposes SiLU into Sigmoid+Multiply, and Sigmoid alone is 78,269,428 cycles for 57 calls (1.37M each) against MB's fused silu_s8 at 84k each -- 75.4M cycles, 55% of ET's ENTIRE 136M excess on yolov8_nano. (2) LAYOUT: XNNPACK runs NHWC inside an NCHW graph so every delegate boundary pays Transpose/Convert -- 1.15M on dronet, 9.8M on yolov8_nano, which MB (NCHW-int8 end to end) does not have at all. Also ET MaxPool is 8.8x SLOWER on dronet (2,097,137 vs 239,338). (3) TIME OUTSIDE THE DELEGATES: 40.5% on dronet, 43.9% on yolov8_nano, and 95.6% on mlp_control -- ExecuTorch interpreter dispatch plus the portable-SCALAR ops the XnnpackPartitioner refused. MB's AOT run_model() has essentially none of this (its mtime wall matches its rdcycle op-sum to ~1%).

platform: AWS F2 f2_quad_hetero_norose_tacit_q31_60mhz, ET on hart 2, same .pte and same baked input in every run
job: fq 851 (clean ITERS=3), fq 857 (identical ELF re-run), fq 853 (profiling ITERS=2 + sampled output), fq 859 (profiling ITERS=2 + LOG_LEVEL=Info)
question: Earlier this session I concluded the yolov8_nano ET-vs-host divergence was requantization rounding, because 100% of the per-element differences were exact integer multiples of the output quantization step. Is that the mechanism?
gates: re-run the IDENTICAL ELF to separate nondeterminism from deterministic divergence
compare across builds that differ ONLY in things that cannot affect arithmetic (log level, whether a debug-print function is compiled in)
verdict: RETRACTED. It is not a rounding convention -- it is a MEMORY bug. Four runs of the same .pte on the same input: mlp_control and dronet return byte-identical checksums in ALL FOUR (14.791794 / -0.030273 / 0.478202). yolov8_nano returns THREE DIFFERENT ANSWERS: fq 851 and fq 857 agree bit-for-bit (same ELF, so it IS deterministic per binary, cycles included); fq 853 gives -449113.776738/-98100.851909/-19073.278003; fq 859 gives -448818.939519/-97843.815654/-19133.433173 -- which MATCHES THE x86 HOST REFERENCE TO ALL SIX PRINTED DIGITS ON ALL THREE OUTPUTS. fq 853 and fq 859 differ ONLY in EXECUTORCH_LOG_LEVEL and whether the MB_ET_SAMPLE_OUTPUT code is compiled in, i.e. pure code-size/layout changes. Deterministic per binary + sensitive to memory layout + one layout exactly right = an uninitialised/stale read or buffer aliasing, NOT arithmetic. That the errors land on exact quantization-step multiples is a CONSEQUENCE of the corrupted value being an int8 that then gets dequantized -- it is not evidence of rounding, and reading it that way was the error.
refuted: The prior-session KernelBench note that 'all checksum mismatches are conv/conv-transposed, likely FP-accumulation-order divergence in XNNPACK conv vs torch' is at least incomplete: on a whole model the same signature is produced by a layout-dependent memory bug, and the FP-accumulation reading cannot explain a build that is host-EXACT.
scope: Confined to yolov8_nano -- the one model of the four whose graph is cut by 8 split_with_sizes_copy and 2 upsample_nearest2d PORTABLE ops between XNNPACK delegates, which is exactly where a delegate-boundary buffer bug would live. mlp_control, dronet and vint match the x86 host to print precision (1.5e-07..4.4e-07) in every run.
impact: yolov8_nano OUTPUTS from this ExecuTorch flow must not be trusted until this is found. yolov8_nano CYCLE COUNTS are unaffected -- fq 857 reproduces fq 851's timings exactly.
next: op-by-op intermediate dump, or poison the ET method_allocation_pool with a non-zero pattern (it is .bss/zeroed today, which is why the bug is deterministic) to make the stale read obvious

platform: AWS F2 f2_quad_hetero_norose_tacit_q31_60mhz, ET pinned to hart 2, pthreadpool=1, MB_XNN_PROFILE=ON
job: fq 861 (LOG_LEVEL=Error + printf profiler) vs fq 859 (LOG_LEVEL=Info + ET_LOG profiler)
question: Two things needed confirming: (a) is the per-op attribution in executorch_perop_where_the_gap_actually_is reproducible across builds, and (b) was fq 859's host-exact yolov8_nano output a one-off?
gates: the two runs must be genuinely independent builds, not a re-run of one ELF
op lines must appear at LOG_LEVEL=Error, which is the whole point of moving them off ET_LOG(Info)
verdict: BOTH CONFIRMED. (a) fq 861 emits 920 op lines at LOG_LEVEL=Error and its per-op sums match fq 859 to within +/-0.8% in every category: mlp_control 67,576 vs 67,226; dronet 8,231,884 vs 8,290,411 (Convolution IGEMM 4,024,595 vs 4,063,025, Max Pooling 2,052,217 vs 2,097,137); yolov8_nano 171,251,378 vs 169,948,067 (Sigmoid 80,210,044 vs 78,269,428, Convolution IGEMM 62,444,587 vs 63,139,893). The delegated-vs-outside split therefore holds. (b) fq 861 reproduces the x86 host reference EXACTLY on all three yolov8_nano outputs (-448818.939519 / -97843.815654 / -19133.433173), independently of fq 859 -- these two builds differ in log level AND in how the profiler emits its lines. So 'profiling ON, sampled-output OFF' is host-exact across two independent builds, while 'profiling ON, sampled-output ON' (fq 853) and 'profiling OFF' (fq 851/857) each diverge, and diverge differently.
sharpens: The distinguishing variable in fq 853 is MB_ET_SAMPLE_OUTPUT -- a printf loop that runs AFTER execute() and only READS output tensors. Code that cannot affect the arithmetic changes the answer. That is a stronger statement of the layout-dependence in executorch_yolov8_result_is_build_layout_dependent_RETRACTION than the log-level argument was.
also: The printf profiler patch is validated as the practical way to profile on FireSim: 38.6 KB uartlog vs 84.5 KB and 1328 s vs ~2640 s, i.e. it removes the risk of hitting the queue timeout that LOG_LEVEL=Info created (fq 859 finished at 44 min against a 50 min limit).

scale_ladder.why: 6 networks against a compile-time NET_A/B/C limit; a generalisation attempt broke the working build and was reverted. Blocker is the per-model source staging and backend_rename mangling loop in harness_microros/CMakeLists.txt, not src/main.c, whose worker is already generic over struct net_ctx.

bug_fixed: HARNESS INFRA, silent workload substitution. period_ms was a uint64_t of INTEGER milliseconds with 0 meaning one-shot, so tight_loop's 0.048 ms and bimodal's 0.032 ms truncated to 0 and those networks ran ONCE instead of periodically -- reported as a successful run of a workload that never happened. Periods are now carried in microseconds end to end: run.sh derives MODEL_PERIODS_US in python (bash has no float arithmetic and CMake's math() is integer-only), CMakeLists surfaces NET_<x>_PERIOD_US, main.c drives every timer from it and tests one_shot against period_us. Verified from compile_commands.json rather than the build log, which does not echo -D flags: NET_B_PERIOD_US=48 and NET_C_PERIOD_US=196 for tight_loop, 32 for bimodal.
characterization_not_a_bug: With sub-millisecond periods now reaching the timer, the rclc executor's real floor is measurable and it is ~1100 us, INDEPENDENT of what is asked: bimodal's 32 us request achieves 1100 us (34x slower) and tight_loop's 48 us request achieves the same 1100 us (23x slower). Same absolute floor, different ratios -- the signature of a fixed per-iteration cost, namely the k_msleep(1) yield in the executor spin loop plus tick granularity, not of per-workload contention. A SECOND sub-millisecond network on the same hart gets nothing at all: tight_loop's mlp_control_sb asked 196 us and completed ZERO iterations while mlp_control_sa took all 30, because the hart is already ~23x oversubscribed before sb asks. Both are honest properties of micro-ROS on this platform, not defects.
consequence: micro-ROS is a usable baseline across the whole workload matrix except scale_ladder, and it cannot represent a control loop faster than ~1 kHz. Any wl_sweep comparison at sub-millisecond periods must quote the ACHIEVED rate, never the requested one.
